title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES ‘SEVA SAMMAN PARV’ AND ‘YUVA PRABODHAN’ ON THE OCCASION OF NUAKHAI FESTIVAL IN RAIPUR
subtitle: IT IS OUR COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY TO RESPECT FOOD, ACKNOWLEDGE THE CONTRIBUTIONS OF OUR FARMERS, AND PROTECT OUR NATURAL RESOURCES: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 6:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced ‘Seva Samman Parv’ and ‘Yuva Prabodhan’ on the occasion of the Nuakhai festival in Raipur, Chhattisgarh today (October 22, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that Nuakhai Milan Samaroh is not merely a cultural celebration; it is a tribute to our rich traditions, social harmony and unity. Such occasions provide us with an opportunity to reconnect with our roots, take pride in our cultural heritage, and pass on the life values to future generations.
The President stated that the Nuakhai festival is a celebration of our agricultural traditions, an expression of gratitude toward nature and a testament to the spirit of community. This festival reminds us that food is not just a means to satisfy hunger; it is a symbol of the hard work of our farmers, the generosity of Mother Earth and the invaluable gifts of nature. She underlined that it is our collective responsibility to respect food, acknowledge the contributions of our farmers, and protect our natural resources.
Addressing the youth present in large numbers, the President said that circumstances may vary, and challenges may differ; yet, youth should possess a deep-seated drive to innovate, to create something better, and to establish their own unique identity. She said that when they align their individual endeavours with collective and national goals, they pave the way for the nation’s progress. She advised them to dream big, broaden their horizons, uphold the highest standards of conduct, and place service to society and the nation at the centre of their endeavours. She encouraged the youth to pursue every endeavour with honesty, integrity and sensitivity. She emphasised that nation-building is not accomplished through major decisions alone, but also through the small, sincere efforts of millions of citizens. She urged them to combine knowledge with humility, ambition with ethical values, and success with a spirit of service, highlighting that these qualities would strengthen their contribution to the vision of a Viksit Bharat.
The President was happy to note the participation of a large number of women in the Nuakhai Milan Samaroh. She said that the nation is moving forward with the goal of a Viksit Bharat by the year 2047. To achieve this goal, the equal participation of women is absolutely essential. She urged all women to participate actively in the affairs of the nation and society. She said that when they progress, the benefits will extend not only to them or their family but to the entire society and the nation. She urged men, especially the youth, to provide an environment for their sisters and daughters in which they can realize their dreams without any barriers. She said that respect for women should not merely be expressed in words; it must be reflected in their behaviour, mindset, and daily conduct.
The President was happy to note that through the efforts of the central and state governments, combined with their own strength of will, the youth of Chhattisgarh have moved away from the path of Naxalism and joined the mainstream. The light of development is now replacing the darkness of terror. She said that this transformation is leading to the well-being of the young people and their families while accelerating the development of the state and the country.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Inaugurates Conference on Cooperative Federalism and Law Reforms in New Delhi
subtitle:
“Legal Reforms Must Keep Pace with Changing Times”: Vice-President Urges States to Repeal Obsolete Laws for Efficient Governance

“The Ultimate Purpose of Law Is to Ensure a Just, Secure and Dignified Life for Every Citizen”: Vice-President

“Strong States Contribute to a Strong Union; Cooperative Governance Transforms Constitutional Ideals into Public Good”: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 1:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the conference on ‘Co-operative Federalism and Law Reforms: National and State Perspective’, organised by the Law Commission of India at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the conference on ‘Co-operative Federalism and Law Reforms: National and State Perspectives’ in New Delhi today. 

Emphasising the spirit of ‘Team India’, he called for greater consultation, coordination and shared responsibility between the Centre and States, noting that political differences must never come in the way of the larger public interest.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 22, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that India’s greatest strength lies in its unity in diversity, with the Constitution providing the framework to balance the strength of the Union with the responsibilities and legitimate autonomy of the States. He emphasised that the true strength of Indian federalism lies in respecting diversity while working towards common national objectives.
Highlighting the importance of cooperative and competitive federalism, the Vice-President said that the vision of ‘Team India’, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, calls for consultation, coordination and shared responsibility between the Centre and the States. He noted that political differences should never come in the way of working together for the larger public interest.
Emphasising the importance of legal reforms in achieving Viksit Bharat @2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that development must be supported by sound laws, transparent institutions, efficient administration and justice for all.
The Vice-President highlighted the replacement of three colonial-era criminal laws and the repeal of over 1,700 obsolete laws in the last twelve years as major steps towards modernising India’s legal framework. He urged State Law Commissions to identify and recommend the amendment or repeal of outdated laws to promote ease of living and efficient governance.
Stressing that cooperative federalism in law reforms does not imply uniformity in every matter, the Vice-President said that the Union and States must work together where their constitutional responsibilities converge, while preserving the States’ legitimate space to address their specific needs. He called for stronger coordination among the Law Commission of India, State Law Commissions and State Law Departments through inter-State consultations, sharing of best practices and systematic review of outdated laws.
Referring to the Sengol installed in Parliament as a symbol of righteous authority and ethical governance, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan invoked the timeless wisdom of Tamil saint-poet Thiruvalluvar on good governance and adherence to the rule of law. He emphasised that good governance, rather than the exercise of power alone, is the foundation of lasting success and prosperity.
The Vice-President expressed hope that the conference would produce concrete and actionable recommendations towards a coherent, responsive and citizen-centric legal framework.
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal; Chairperson of the Law Commission of India, Justice Dinesh Maheshwari; Member Secretary, Law Commission of India, Dr. Anju Rathi Rana; and Member of the Law Commission of India, Prof. D. P. Verma, were among the dignitaries present on the occasion.

title: Prime Minister Shri  Narendra Modi addresses the NDTV World Summit 2026 in New Delhi
subtitle:
The changing world order calls for stronger global institutions, a greater voice for the Global South and international cooperation that stands firm in times of crisis: PM

Viksit Bharat is not just a promise for its people, but a guarantee of a better world: PM

India is strengthening its own capabilities to help strengthen the world: PM

India is now collaborating with the world not merely as a back office, but as a brain office: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 9:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri  Narendra Modi today addressed the NDTV World Summit 2026 in New Delhi. Greeting the international delegates amidst the joyous festive season in the country, the Prime Minister welcomed the participants to the summit. He commended the gathering for deliberating on serious global matters.
Highlighting the timely relevance of the NDTV summit's deliberations, the Prime Minister noted that discussions regarding a new world order have become ubiquitous because global shifts now directly impact the daily lives of ordinary citizens. He emphasized that these real-world repercussions elevate the necessity of such international forums."In such a scenario, the importance of such world summits increases even more,” observed PM Modi.
Framing the central debate around 'The World Between Orders', the Prime Minister stated that the global community must fundamentally examine why the existing order is shifting and why legacy systems are failing to resolve contemporary crises. He added that answering these questions naturally leads to examining the nation's specific responsibilities on the world stage."And second, what is India's role in this changing world?” noted Shri Modi.
Tracing the organic evolution of international relations since the Second World War, the Prime Minister recalled how the United Nations was founded on the realization that dialogue and cooperation must supersede raw power, yet Global Institutions failed to adapt as new economies, technologies, and nations outside the original decision-making table rose to prominence. Pointing out that erstwhile connectors like trade, technology, and sea routes have now morphed into arenas of weaponization, conflict, and geopolitical tension, he stressed that the modern imperative is to build an inclusive order that bridges the gap between institutional decision-making and current realities."And right from here, the question of India's role comes to the fore,” asserted PM Modi.
Recalling the deep global divisions, mutual suspicion, and trust deficit during the COVID-19 pandemic when champions of globalization prioritized self-interest, the Prime Minister reminded the audience of his 2020 appeal from the G20 platform to build a new world order focused on the collective well-being of humankind and centered around humanity. He also reiterated his message from the UNGA platform that same year regarding the urgent necessity of institutional evolution. “If the century changes and we do not change, then our capacity to bring change also weakens,” asserted Shri Modi.
Questioning the exact architecture of the emerging global framework, the Prime Minister emphasized the urgent need to reform multilateral institutions and accord due space to the voice of the Global South. He insisted that international cooperation must extend beyond favorable periods to remain resilient during severe crises."For this, having an effective consensus among all stakeholders is essential,” affirmed PM Modi.
Quoting Chanakya’s Arthashastra on how a weak system breeds Matsya Nyaya,where the big fish swallows the small,the Prime Minister stated that the nation's core vision is to prevent such predatory global dynamics. He pointed to the pandemic as tangible proof of this philosophy, recalling how the country stepped up to supply vaccines and medicines to over 100 nations while wealthier countries looked inward."The world needs such a system that prevents the situation of Matsya Nyaya from arising,” asserted Shri Modi.
Operating on the foundational mantra of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, the Prime Minister highlighted how the nation has cemented its role as a Vishwa-Bandhu. He noted that despite widespread skepticism regarding the possibility of reaching consensus during India's hosting of the G20 and BRICS Summits, the country successfully built bridges across antagonistic divides to deliver unanimous Delhi Declarations both times."This is the trust in India's role as a Vishwa-Bandhu,” affirmed PM Modi.
Linking the nation's growing strength directly to global welfare, the Prime Minister explained that because domestic policies are anchored in timeless civilizational values rather than fleeting impulses, a stronger India guarantees global stability and continuity. Recalling his recent 'Power to Empower' vision, he emphasized that a self-reliant, economically robust, and skilled Viksit Bharat naturally fortifies global supply chains, drives productivity, and inspires worldwide prosperity."Meaning, India today is increasing its capability so that the capability of the world can also increase,” asserted Shri Modi.
Reiterating the nation's relentless drive to become a top-three global economy, the Prime Minister noted that emerging as the fastest-growing major economy amidst severe international headwinds further boosts national morale. He proudly listed the country's premier global standing across green energy, Artificial Intelligence, startups, and the digital economy."India is number one in real-time digital payments,” noted PM Modi.
Spotlighting a series of historic technological and environmental milestones achieved for the very first time, the Prime Minister highlighted the Fast Breeder Reactor achieving criticality, the integration of digital technology into the national Census, and the inaugural run of a hydrogen train. He also pointed to the monumental leap in the nation's clean energy transition."For the first time, India crossed the figure of 300 gigawatts in Non-fossil Electricity Capacity,” observed Shri Modi.
Sharing insights from his recent interaction with the victorious Asian Games contingent that secured 85 medals, the Prime Minister celebrated several unprecedented sporting feats. He lauded the women's recurve archery team for winning maiden team and individual golds, alongside Indian pugilists clinching three boxing gold medals in a single edition for the first time in history.
Engaging the audience with a mention of the unique sport of Sepak Takraw, a net-based discipline combining elements of football and volleyball played entirely with the feet,the Prime Minister noted how global competitors have long won laurels in the game. He proudly announced that Indian athletes broke new ground in this unconventional sport during the recent Asian Games."For the first time, in the recent Asian Games, India has also won a medal in an event of this sport,  the Men's Quadrant,” noted Shri Modi.
Characterizing these diverse breakthroughs as the hallmark of a transforming nation, the Prime Minister stated that the country is simultaneously fortifying its traditional strengths while emerging as a formidable force in entirely new domains. He emphasized that these sweeping achievements are not isolated occurrences, but the direct outcome of a deliberate governance framework."All this is the result of the policy of Reform, Perform, and Transform,” asserted PM Modi.
The Prime Minister highlighted the transformative power of collective national willpower. He remarked that when a determined nation marches forward, its foundational infrastructure becomes a symbol of resilience rather than vulnerability."Rather, that very power grid elevates the progress and self-confidence of the country,” observed Shri Modi.
Praising the high spirits of the youth, women, farmers, fishermen, the poor, and the middle class in building a Viksit Bharat, the Prime Minister cited a 25 percent surge in September goods and products exports and the more-than-doubling of seafood exports over 12 years. He also noted that over 3.5 crore Lakhpati Didis have been created in villages while the government works on the target of creating 6 crore Lakhpati Didis, alongside the generation of 70 lakh new jobs under the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana and zero tax on incomes up to 12 lakh rupees for the middle class. “Ease of Living is improving in the country and new opportunities for employment are also being created,” affirmed PM Modi.
Reflecting on the nation's evolution from being merely the 'World’s Back Office' and a basic service provider, the Prime Minister stated that the country is now actively innovating, designing, and building original technologies for the globe. He pointed out that the nation ranks third globally in research publications and witnessed nearly 1.5 lakh patent filings in 2025 alone."Regarding research and innovation, this is a glimpse of the possibilities in India,” noted Shri Modi.
Spotlighting the domestic semiconductor ecosystem, the Prime Minister observed that 20 percent of the global chip-design workforce resides in the country, with Indian engineers actively designing cutting-edge 2-to-3 nanometer chips. He added that comprehensive facilities are being provided to expand this talent pool across academic institutions."Our students have prepared more than three hundred and twenty-five Chip Designs so far,” noted PM Modi.
Pointing out that India hosts over half of the world's Global Capability Centres, the Prime Minister explained that these hubs have pivoted from basic support services to advanced AI, cloud computing, engineering, analytics, and product development. He declared that as the world shifts its trust from Indian manpower to Indian mind-power, the nation has transitioned from 'Talent at Scale' to 'Thinking at Scale'."We are now working with the world not just as a Back Office, but also as a Brain Office,” asserted Shri Modi.
Explaining the strategic foresight behind government policies and long-term investments designed to build domestic capacities, reduce foreign dependency, and prepare for future crises, the Prime Minister cited the pharmaceutical sector's historical reliance on imported raw materials. He detailed how bringing essential antibiotic precursor Penicillin G under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme successfully revived its domestic manufacturing after a decades-long halt."Now, in Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, after many years, the domestic production of Penicillin G has restarted,” observed PM Modi.
Expanding on pharmaceutical self-reliance beyond Penicillin G, the Prime Minister stated that the government is constructing a complete domestic supply chain for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) through the PLI framework. He noted that this targeted policy intervention has already attracted over 5,000 crore rupees in investments across nearly 40 operational projects."Such policies and decisions are taking India towards self-reliance,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Concluding his address by focusing on the grand goal of a Viksit Bharat powered by the limitless aspirations of 140 crore citizens and the resonant spirit of 'We Will Do It', the Prime Minister pledged to innovate, forge new paths, turn challenges into opportunities, and link India's success with global prosperity. He expressed full confidence that the insights generated at the summit would energize national resolutions, offering his final best wishes to all participants."We will dream big, we will turn every challenge into an opportunity, and we will take every resolution to fulfillment,” affirmed PM Modi.

title: English rendering of PM's address in NDTV World Summit
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 9:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Greetings to all of you! This is the festive season; the nation is filled with celebration, enthusiasm, and energy. In this atmosphere of joy and celebration, I welcome and greet all of you friends who have come here from all over the world.
Friends,
This NDTV summit is dedicated to deliberating on serious matters. Nowadays, everyone is talking about a new world order. Because this affects ordinary life, the importance of such world summits increases even more.
Friends
When talking about 'The World Between Orders', we need to understand two things. First, why is the world order changing? Why is the old global order unable to provide solutions to today's challenges? And second, what is India's role in this changing world?
Friends,
If I elaborate on the first point, this change is natural and spontaneous. The Second World War taught the world a major lesson. The world realized that a global order cannot function merely on the basis of power and self-interest. Dialogue is essential, cooperation is necessary, and resolving disputes is equally vital. It was this sentiment that laid the foundation of the United Nations, or the UN. For decades, the UN played a significant role in promoting global cooperation and peace. But with time, the world kept changing. New aspirations emerged. New economies and new powers arose. The challenges confronting the world also became far more complex than ever before. Technology transformed society, the economy, and the very nature of power. And countries that were not at the table when the global order was initially established came forward with their own prominent roles. The question then arises: did the global order change at the same pace? The answer is no. Neither did the world order change, nor could global institutions adapt themselves with equivalent speed. The United Nations and other global institutions have had their historic role. Yet in the face of today’s challenges, their limitations are clearly visible. Now, emerging powers are rising. New voices are demanding their rightful place. New challenges demand new solutions. When the reality of the world shifts, but decision-making methods remain unchanged, a gap begins to widen between the system and reality. That is precisely what we are witnessing today. For decades, trade connected nations, technology closed distances, maritime routes linked economies, and culture and mobility brought diverse societies closer together; but today, these very links face fresh strains. Trade is being weaponized. Technology is turning into a new arena of competition and conflict. Sea routes are emerging as epicenters of geopolitical tension. Therefore, the challenge today is not merely about the emergence of a new global order. The real challenge is: in a changing world, how do we build an order where new realities find their place, global institutions become more effective, and the spirit of cooperation among nations is reinforced? And this is where the question of India's role comes to the fore.
Friends,
Before elaborating on India's role, I will take you back by 7 to 8 years. What transpired during the COVID pandemic is something we all witnessed. When the world needed cooperation the most, it appeared completely divided. Those who made grand proclamations about globalization prioritized their own self-interests in a time of crisis. In that era of fragmentation, everyone viewed each other with suspicion, and global trust had hit rock bottom; it was then, in 2020, from the G20 platform, that I placed an idea before the world, calling for "a new world order for the collective well-being of humankind" - an order with humanity at its very core. That same year, from the UNGA platform, I said, "If the century changes and we do not, our ability to bring about change also weakens."
Friends,
Today, while it is true that the world order is changing, the real question is: as the old global order shifts, what kind of new world order do we want to build together? Reforms in multilateral institutions are essential. It is vital to grant the Global South its rightful place and voice. International cooperation must not be reserved only for good times; it must remain effective during crises, and for this, meaningful consensus among all stakeholders is imperative.
Friends,
In our heritage, Chanakya stated in the Arthashastra: ‘Apranitah tu matsya-nyayam ud-bhavayati’ - meaning, when governance weakens, the "law of the fish" (matsya nyaya) takes over. Under matsya nyaya, the big fish swallows the smaller fish. The world needs a system that prevents such a situation from arising. That is India's vision, and that is precisely what India is doing. The world experienced this role of India during the severe crisis of the pandemic. When capable nations were thinking solely of themselves, India stepped forward, delivered vaccines to every needy nation, and dispatched medicines to over 100 countries.
Friends,
Guided by the principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’, India is performing its duty as a Vishwa-Bandhu (universal friend). You have witnessed this firsthand: the G20 Summit was held under India’s presidency, and the BRICS Summit was held under India’s leadership. How many doubts were voiced regarding both summits? It was said that building consensus on joint declarations would be impossible. But India built bridges, emphasized dialogue, and on both occasions, the Delhi Declaration was adopted through unanimous consensus. Nations considered bitter rivals came together on India’s platform. This is not mere coincidence. This is the trust placed in India’s role as a Vishwa-Bandhu.
Friends,
The stronger and more empowered India becomes, the greater the benefit to humanity. This is because India's policies and decisions are inspired by timeless experience and civilizational values. India does not make decisions driven by fleeting moments. Hence, India is a guarantee of stability and an assurance of continuity. Our resolve for a Viksit Bharat (Developed India) also fosters this very spirit. Just a few days ago at a summit, I presented the vision of "Power to Empower." A developed India is not just for ourselves; it is a guarantee for a better world. When India advances toward self-reliance, it strengthens global supply chains. When India's economy grows stronger, it provides hope of prosperity to the world. When India’s youth become capable and skilled, it inspires global confidence in innovation and productivity. In other words, India is enhancing its own capabilities today so that the world’s capacity can also increase.
Friends,
India is working with all its might to become a top-3 economy. Our confidence grows even further when we look at the present difficult global circumstances, in the midst of which India continues to emerge as the fastest-growing major economy. Today, India is among the top economies in green energy. India ranks among the top three AI ecosystems. India is among the top three startup ecosystems. India is one of the largest digital economies. India stands number one in real-time digital payments.
Friends,
Today's India is expanding its capabilities across various sectors, and there are numerous milestones achieved for the first time in the country. India's Fast Breeder Reactor achieved criticality for the first time. India linked the Census with digital technology for the first time. During this period, India’s first hydrogen train began operations, and India crossed the 300-gigawatt mark in non-fossil electricity capacity for the first time.
Friends,
I will give you another example. A few days ago, I had the opportunity to meet young athletes returning from the Asian Games. India won 85 medals this time, achieving many milestones for the first time. The women’s recurve archery team won team and individual gold medals for the first time. In boxing, India won three gold medals in a single Asian Games, which is also a first.
Friends,
Now I will mention a term, and I hope many people in the hall have heard it. The word is - Sepak Takraw. Sepak Takraw, have you heard this word? For those who do not know, let me tell you that it is the name of a sport. The world plays it and has been winning medals in it. It is essentially a hybrid combination of football and volleyball. It is played with the feet, but the action takes place across a net. India won a medal for the first time in recent Asian Games in an event of this sport - the Men’s Quadrant.
Friends,
This is the hallmark of a changing India. In every sector, something new and unprecedented is taking place. That means India's conventional strengths are being reinforced, and where we were once not as strong, we are emerging as a new force. None of this is happening in isolation; it is the direct outcome of the policy of 'Reform, Perform, Transform'.
Friends,
The country has seen days when the entire power grid would collapse under rising electricity demand. But when a nation rises with sheer willpower and sets forth, the power grid does not collapse; instead, that very grid fuels the nation's progress and soaring confidence.
Friends,
Today, our youth power, women power, our farmers, fishermen, the poor, and the middle class are engaged with high spirits in the building of a Viksit Bharat. Look around today: India's exports are setting new records. Speaking of September alone, exports of goods and products increased by nearly 25 percent compared to last year. Seafood exports have more than doubled in the last 12 years. In our villages, more than 3.5 crore women have become Lakhpati Didis, and we are working toward the goal of creating 6 crore Lakhpati Didis. Under the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana, around 70 lakh new jobs have been created in a very short span of time. For the middle class, income tax has been made zero up to 12 lakh rupees - this needs to be reminded to you again and again; it cannot be that you simply take what you get and forget it. Ease of Living is improving across the country, and new employment opportunities are being generated.
Friends,
There was a time when the world referred to India as the 'World’s Back Office', but today's India is not merely a service provider; we are innovating, designing, and creating new solutions and technologies for the world. Look at the field of research alone: today we rank third in research publications. In the year 2025, nearly 1.5 lakh patents were filed - 1.5 lakh patents in a single year. This offers a glimpse into the immense potential for research and innovation in India.
Friends,
Consider the semiconductor sector as well: nearly 20 percent of the world’s chip-design workforce is in India. Indian engineers within the country are working on advanced 2 to 3-nanometer chip designs. To expand this talent pool further, every necessary facility is being provided in the country today. In Indian academic institutions, our students have designed more than 325 chips so far.
Friends,
Another example is Global Capability Centres. More than half of the world’s capability centres are located in India. It is not just about the numbers; the nature of their work is changing. Previously, many centres focused solely on support services. Today, they operate across fields like AI, Cloud, Engineering, Analytics, and Product Development. In other words, India’s role is shifting, and India’s identity is evolving. We have moved from 'Talent at Scale' to 'Thinking at Scale'. The world that once trusted India’s manpower now places equal trust in India’s mind-power. As a result, we are working alongside the world not merely as a Back Office, but as a Brain Office.
Friends,
Whenever the government frames a policy or takes an investment decision in any sector, there is clear thinking behind it: what capacities India needs to develop, in which domains we must reduce dependence on other nations, and which impending crises we must prepare for today. We keep these factors in mind with every decision. There are many investments whose benefits take years to become visible, but they hold immense significance for the nation's future. Let me share an interesting example. All of you are familiar with India's pharmaceutical capabilities, but until a few years ago, India relied heavily on imports for raw materials and medicines. Now the country is changing this situation. You must have heard of Penicillin G, which is essential for antibiotics. Over the last two to three decades, its domestic production in India had practically ceased. We brought it under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme. Today, after many years, domestic production of Penicillin G has resumed in Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh.
Friends,
Penicillin G is just one example. In India, we are building an entire domestic supply chain for APIs (Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients) - the fundamental raw materials for medicine manufacturing. That is why this sector was brought under the PLI scheme, attracting over 5,000 crore rupees in investment so far, with around 40 projects already underway. Such policies and decisions are steering India toward self-reliance.
Friends,
Amidst discussions of so many national achievements, our media friends might complain that while much was said, nothing was spoken about their work. NDTV is hosting such a magnificent event, and our motto is ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’ - which includes the development of the media - so perhaps you would appreciate a few candid and sweet-and-sour remarks as well?
Friends,
While the world is searching for a new order, some people are dreaming of disorder in India. Today, when there is so much disarray in the world, the image of a strong India should be conveyed globally. Yet these individuals are bent on tarnishing India's reputation. They travel abroad to defame India and plead for foreign intervention. One wonders how long Congress will continue to wager the nation's interests just to launch its failed product. In an entire year, Sriharikota does not attempt as many launches as Congress makes failed attempts to launch its leader.
Friends,
Whatever decline Congress chooses to bring upon itself is entirely its own concern, and we have no problem with that. But to protect one family from the repeated stain of failure, Congress is putting India's achievements, strengths, and progress on trial. The grapes are so sour that Congress has set about cutting down the grapevine itself. In reality, this family has become a burden on their party; senior elders of the party understand this and even share it with us in private, yet they swallow their humiliation and remain silent.
Friends,
This conduct of Congress harms honest critics of the government as well, and this imposes a huge cost in a democracy. Honest critics suffer immensely because of this. Those who wish to present their critique against the government in a democratic manner find their voices drowned out by Congress's clamour; the voices of genuine critics are suppressed. Those who genuinely care for democracy and the national interest—even if they are staunch opponents of the government—find no opportunity to speak amidst the shouting and screeching of Congress. We have seen in Parliament: there are so many talented young Members of Parliament from opposition parties who wish to put forward their views and critique the government, but Congress disrupts Parliament so that others do not get an opportunity, simply because Congress wants to keep only one person in the limelight. By doing so, Congress does a grave injustice to the young MPs of the opposition.
And friends,
Movements that organically aim to highlight the government’s shortcomings and genuinely seek systemic reform—which is indeed necessary in a democracy—are also ruined by Congress. Congress has become a parasite that does not want anyone else to progress. Intellectual Naxals have captured Congress's mind to such an extent that Congress has lost its own capacity to think. Those who once wrought destruction in forests have infiltrated Congress and are now bent on wreaking havoc on the country.
Friends,
Amidst all these challenges, the grand goal of a Viksit Bharat stands before us. The nation's aspirations are boundless. Therefore, a single spirit resonates across India today, and that spirit is: 'We Will Do It, We Will Do It.' We will dream big, turn every challenge into an opportunity, and translate every resolution into reality. Our strength is our self-confidence; our inspiration lies in the dreams of 140 crore fellow citizens. We will innovate, forge new paths, reach new heights, and link India's success with the world's success. I am confident that the nectar emerging from this summit will empower this very spirit, infuse our resolutions with new energy, and play a vital role in realizing India's grand aspirations. Once again, my warmest wishes to all of you.
Thank you very much.

content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at 11 AM on 23 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
The three-day Sammelan, being held from 23 to 25 October 2026, will bring together over 9,000 participants from India and abroad. It marks the culmination of the year-long celebrations commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission, a global spiritual movement founded by Swami Chinmayananda in 1951 to make the wisdom of Vedanta and the Bhagavad Gita accessible to all. Over the decades, the Mission has expanded its work across spiritual education, cultural preservation, youth empowerment and community service.
The year-long celebrations began last year with the Prime Minister releasing a Tamil versification of the Bhagavad Gita, produced by Chinmaya Mission with music by Ilaiyaraaja, at Gangaikonda Cholapuram in Tamil Nadu. Several initiatives and events were organised during the year, including mass havans at multiple locations, consecration of the Maa Soundarya Chinmayi Temple in Tripura, and Chinmaya Gita Samarpanam under which over 1 lakh people across the world chanted the 15th chapter of the Bhagavad Gita together online. A major initiative of the celebrations was Gita Panchamrit, centred on five select verses of the Bhagavad Gita. To take the message of the Gita across the country, 15 young members of Chinmaya Yuva Kendra undertook the Chinmaya Amrit Yatra, travelling over 40,000 km across the country.

title: India-Poland Joint Statement
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 3:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
At the invitation of the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of the Republic of Poland, H.E. Mr. Donald Tusk, paid an official visit to India from 21-23 October 2026. Prime Minister Tusk was accompanied by a high-level delegation, including around 100 leading CEOs and industry representatives.
Prime Minister Modi and Prime Minister Tusk held comprehensive discussions on bilateral, regional and global issues of mutual interest.
The Prime Ministers recalled Prime Minister Modi’s landmark visit to Poland in August 2024, when the bilateral relationship was elevated to a Strategic Partnership and the India-Poland Action Plan for 2024-2028 was adopted. They endorsed the mid-term review of the Action Plan done by the Indian External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar and the Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski in Warsaw in September 2026.
The Prime Ministers noted that the present visit imparts fresh momentum to the Strategic Partnership and reaffirmed their determination to translate this partnership into concrete, time-bound and mutually beneficial outcomes.
The Leaders agreed to intensify high-level political exchanges and institutional dialogue, and encouraged closer engagement between their Parliaments, state and regional authorities, think tanks and policy institutions.
The Prime Ministers underlined the importance of the historic India-EU Summit on 27 January 2026 in New Delhi, the Towards 2030: A Joint India-European Union Comprehensive Strategic Agenda, the conclusion of the EU-India Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and the Comprehensive Framework of Cooperation on Mobility. On the FTA, they called for its early signing and ratification as well as timely implementation, with a view to unlocking new opportunities for trade and investment, diversifying and strengthening critical value chains, and opening new markets.
Trade, Economic Cooperation and Investment
Prime Minister of India congratulated Poland on crossing the USD 1 trillion GDP mark and noted the resilience and dynamism of the Polish economy. Poland appreciated India’s record as the fastest growing big economy and its impressive trajectory to become a USD 10 trillion economy in the coming years. The Leaders recognised the complementary strengths of the two economies and the opportunities arising from India’s and Poland’s respective growth paths.
The Leaders set the target of doubling bilateral trade by 2030. Prime Minister of India invited Polish companies to expand their investments and operations in India and to benefit from India’s large market, skilled workforce and growing manufacturing and innovation ecosystem. Prime Minister Tusk appreciated Indian investment in Poland and highlighted Poland’s strength as a gateway for Indian businesses seeking to expand their presence in Central and Eastern Europe and the wider European market.
Leaders agreed to expand cooperation in agriculture by resuming the activities of the bilateral working group, aimed at intensifying bilateral trade and cooperation.
The Leaders welcomed the India-Poland Business Forum held during the visit with the presence of leading CEOs and industry representatives from both countries. They encouraged businesses to explore partnerships in sectors including industrial machinery, defence, infrastructure, pharmaceuticals, mining and critical minerals, energy, ICT and other areas of mutual interest.
The Leaders underscored the importance of resilient and diversified supply chains, promotion of medium and small enterprises, innovation-led growth and digital transformation. They recognised the transformative role of digital technologies and artificial intelligence in economic growth, productivity and public service delivery. Acknowledging the India-EU Comprehensive Strategic Agenda, both leaders also agreed to undertake collaborative research on AI, semiconductors and Quantum technologies as well as to enhance Startup partnerships. They agreed to encourage closer cooperation between enterprises, research institutions and innovation ecosystems in both countries.
Defence and Security Cooperation
The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening defence and security cooperation. They welcomed the outcomes of the 8th meeting of the Joint Working Group on Defence, held in Warsaw in September 2026, and agreed to maintain regular exchanges between the defence establishments of both countries.
The Leaders welcomed growing interaction between Indian and Polish defence industries and encouraged them to identify commercially viable areas of cooperation. A Defence Industry Dialogue was proposed by the leaders to encourage the development of a forward-looking framework for defence industrial cooperation, including greater business-to-business engagement and, where mutually agreed, partnerships in technology, co-development, co-production and other forms of industrial collaboration.
Both leaders welcomed the signing of the India-EU Security and Defence Partnership in January 2026 and underlined the importance of strengthening India-Poland cooperation in critical and emerging technologies, cybersecurity and defence innovation, including through business and other platforms, contributing to enhanced technological resilience and closer India-EU security and defence cooperation.
Both sides underlined the importance of having an Agreement on Mutual Protection and Exchange of Classified Information and expressed their expectation that it would be signed soon.
Space Cooperation / New technologies
The Leaders recognised cooperation in the space sector as a key element of the Strategic Partnership and encouraged stronger institutional and industry-level engagement, welcoming efforts to identify concrete areas of mutually beneficial cooperation.
Both Leaders highlighted opportunities of close cooperation on semiconductors.
The Prime Ministers emphasised the potential for collaboration in circular economy and recovery industry, particularly focusing on recycling of batteries and refining of rare earth minerals.
They underlined opportunities for closer cooperation in geology, mining and critical minerals sector. An MoU in this regard is under negotiation.
Connectivity, maritime and shipping
The Leaders welcomed the prospect of exploring the opportunities for enhancing direct flights on the routes between Poland and India. They encouraged the civil aviation/ aeronautical authorities to hold direct talks as a symbol of strengthening bilateral relations.
Both sides highlighted the prospect of cooperation in the shipping industry as well as in maritime security.
The Leaders recognised the importance of cooperation between ports in advancing a secure, resilient, and integrated network that diversifies global supply chains, shortens transit times, and safeguards critical infrastructure against geopolitical disruptions. The two leaders noted the importance of improving connectivity, including through the India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) initiative.
The Prime Ministers agreed on developing scientific cooperation in polar affairs.
Science, Education and Academic Cooperation
The Leaders noted Poland’s long tradition of scholarship in Indology and Sanskrit and welcomed the ICCR Chair of Indian Studies at the Jagiellonian University in Kraków. They acknowledged the presence of Polish language teachers at Indian universities. They also noted the extensive network of cooperation between Indian and Polish higher education institutions and encouraged deeper institutional partnerships, student and faculty exchanges, and called for more collaborative research.
Culture and People-to-People Ties
The Leaders reaffirmed that strong people-to-people ties are an important pillar of the Strategic Partnership. They welcomed growing exchanges between the two peoples, including among professionals and tourists and agreed to encourage cultural cooperation, including sports, youth exchanges and tourism. An agreement on cooperation in the fields of culture, science and higher education will be concluded soon. A Cooperation agreement between the National Archives of India and General Director of the State Archives of the Republic of Poland was concluded and would be signed soon.
Both sides acknowledged that the memorial of the Maharaja Jamsaheb (popularly known as the Good Maharaja in Poland) and the Principality of Kolhapur in Warsaw represent a living bridge between the people of the two friendly countries and an evocative chapter of history, where India provided a home to thousands of Polish women and children during World War-II. Both sides expressed satisfaction that two editions of the Jam Saheb Memorial Youth Exchange Programme had taken place, including most recently in October 2026.
Both sides recalled with appreciation the assistance provided by the Polish authorities to more than 2,000 Indian students stranded in Ukraine under Operation Ganga.
Multilateral Cooperation and Global Issues
The Leaders underlined the importance of multilateralism with the UN Charter at its core. Both sides agreed that the United Nations needs structural reforms, including through the expansion of the UN Security Council in both permanent and non-permanent categories in order to stay relevant, credible and effective. The Polish side expressed its support for India’s membership of a more inclusive, reformed and expanded UNSC, as well as reiterated its support for India’s candidature for a non-permanent seat in the UNSC for 2028-29.
The Leaders highlighted the role of the G20 as a key forum for international cooperation. They expressed their readiness to cooperate in the G20 tracks and workstreams in which the Republic of Poland participates or may be invited to participate.
The two leaders expressed their deepest concern over the war raging in Ukraine, including its terrible and tragic humanitarian consequences. They reiterated the need for a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace in line with international law, consistent with the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, including respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity. They also noted the negative impacts of the war in Ukraine with regard to global food and energy security, especially for the Global South.
The two leaders unequivocally condemned terrorism and violent extremism leading to terrorism in all their forms and manifestations, irrespective of their motivations, including cross-border terrorism, and stressed that there can be no justification for terrorism on any grounds. They condemned in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir on 22 April 2025. They called for strong and concerted action against terrorists and terrorist entities including those designated by the UNSC 1267 sanctions committee. Both sides also called upon all countries to continue to work towards eliminating terrorist safe havens and infrastructure as well as to disrupt terrorism financing networks. Both leaders called for the early adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism (CCIT) at the United Nations. They agreed to have a dialogue on counter-terrorism.
The Leaders reaffirmed the importance of a free, open, peaceful and prosperous Indo-Pacific and of respect for international law, including the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). They underscored the importance of freedom of navigation and the peaceful resolution of disputes in accordance with international law. India invited Poland to join the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI).
Both Leaders welcomed the first Foreign Ministers' Meetings of India and the Visegrad Group (V4), comprising Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic and the Slovak Republic. They reaffirmed their commitment to strengthen cooperation through the V4+India format and to build a forward-looking partnership based on shared interests and complementarities.
The Leaders underscored the need for accelerated global action on climate change, and reaffirmed their support for the UNFCCC process and the Paris Agreement. They recognised the growing risks posed by extreme weather events, environmental degradation and biodiversity loss and encouraged closer bilateral cooperation in clean energy, sustainable technologies and climate-resilient development. They highlighted the need to increase the share of home-grown clean energy in national energy mixes to enhance energy security, protect the climate, and improve industrial competitiveness. India welcomed Poland’s announcement of joining the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI). India invited Poland to join the International Solar Alliance and the Global Biofuels Alliance.
Prime Minister Tusk thanked Prime Minister Modi for the warm hospitality extended to him and his delegation. The Leaders reaffirmed their shared commitment to further deepen and diversify the India-Poland Strategic Partnership and to ensure effective implementation of the Action Plan (2024-2028) through regular high-level engagement and strengthened institutional cooperation.
Prime Minister Tusk also extended an invitation to Prime Minister Modi to visit Poland.

content:
Your Excellency, Mr. Prime Minister
दोनों देशों के delegates,
मीडिया के साथियों,
नमस्कार!
पोलैंड के प्रधानमंत्री जी का भारत में हार्दिक स्वागत करते हुए मुझे बहुत खुशी हो रही है।
2024 में मेरी पोलैंड यात्रा के दौरान उन्होंने मेरा और मेरे डेलिगेशन का आत्मीय स्वागत किया था। उस यात्रा में हमने अपने संबंधों को Strategic Partnership का दर्जा दिया।
इसी मजबूत आधार पर, पिछले दो वर्षों में हमारी साझेदारी ने नई गति पकड़ी है। और आज प्रधानमंत्री जी के साथ हुई बैठक में, हमने अपनी Strategic Partnership को और सुदृढ़ करने के लिए कई महत्वपूर्ण निर्णय लिए हैं।
Friends,
भारत और पोलैंड की मित्रता केवल कूटनीतिक संबंधों पर नहीं, बल्कि मानवता और संवेदना की साझी विरासत पर आधारित है।
द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के दौरान जामनगर और कोल्हापुर के राजपरिवारों ने, पोलैंड के हजारों बच्चों और परिवारों को भारत में आश्रय दिया था। आज भी पोलैंड के लोग जाम साहब को बड़े सम्मान से “दोब्री महाराजा”, यानी “Good Maharaja” के नाम से याद करते हैं।
2022 में यूक्रेन से हमारे स्टूडेंट्स की सुरक्षित वापसी में सहयोग देकर, पोलैंड ने भी मानवता की इसी भावना को आगे बढ़ाया। मुझे खुशी है कि जाम साहब यूथ एक्सचेंज प्रोग्राम के माध्यम से, पोलैंड के युवा भारत आ रहे हैं और हमारी ऐतिहासिक मित्रता को नई पीढ़ी तक ले जा रहे हैं।
Friends,
आज विश्व अनिश्चितता और बदलाव के दौर से गुजर रहा है। ऐसे समय में भी भारत और पोलैंड, दोनों ही ग्रोथ, टेक्नॉलजी और इनोवेशन के महत्वपूर्ण केंद्र के रूप में उभर रहे हैं।
पिछले वर्ष पोलैंड की GDP ने एक ट्रिलियन डॉलर का ऐतिहासिक पड़ाव पार किया। इसके लिए मैं प्रधानमंत्री जी को बहुत बहुत बधाई देता हूँ। वहीं, भारत ने भी पिछले क्वार्टर में 7.8% की शानदार ग्रोथ दर्ज की है।
हमारी बढ़ती आर्थिक ताकत ने भारत-पोलैंड साझेदारी के लिए नए अवसर पैदा किए हैं। और भारत-यूरोपियन यूनियन Free Trade Agreement ने इन अवसरों को और व्यापक बनाया है। इस समझौते के लागू होने पर भारत से पोलैंड को, मशीनरी, केमिकल्स, प्लास्टिक्स और इंजीनियरिंग गुड्स के निर्यात के नए अवसर खुलेंगे। साथ-ही, रेलवे और मोबिलिटी, एडवांस्ड मैन्युफैक्चरिंग, फूड प्रोसेसिंग और बायो-टेक जैसे क्षेत्रों में हम पोलैंड से नए निवेश आकर्षित करेंगे।
मुझे विशेष खुशी है कि प्रधानमंत्री जी एक बड़े बिज़नेस डेलिगेशन के साथ भारत आए हैं। हमें विश्वास है कि दोनों देशों की कंपनियाँ मिलकर विश्व के लिए trusted supply chains विकसित करेंगी, और 2030 तक द्विपक्षीय व्यापार को दोगुना करने के हमारे साझा लक्ष्य को भी साकार करेंगी।
Friends,
आज हमने डिफेन्स, स्पेस और न्यूक्लियर एनर्जी में संबंधों को प्रगाढ़ करने पर सहमति बनाई है। इन सभी स्ट्रैटीजिक क्षेत्रों में हम पोलैंड की कम्पनीज़ को भारत के साथ co-development और co-production करने के लिए आमंत्रित करते हैं।
क्रिटिकल मिनरल्स और कोल गैसिफिकेशन में भी, हम पोलैंड की एक्स्पर्टीज़ को साथ लेकर नई साझेदारियाँ विकसित करेंगे।
IT और साइबर सिक्योरिटी में हमारे संबंध पहले से ही मजबूत हैं। कई भारतीय IT कम्पनीज़ पोलैंड में काम कर रही हैं।इस सहयोग को आगे बढ़ाते हुए, हमने भारत-पोलैंड start-up bridge स्थापित करने पर सहमति बनाई है।
हम दोनों देशों के युवाओं के बीच टेक्नॉलजी hackathons भी आयोजित करेंगे। इन पहलों से AI, साइबर, फिन-टेक और अन्य emerging technologies में हमारे सहयोग को नई गति मिलेगी, और दोनों देशों के युवाओं के लिए नए अवसर पैदा होंगे।
Friends,
कल्चरल और People-to-people ties हमारे संबंधों की सबसे बड़ी ताकत हैं। हमें बहुत खुशी है कि पोलैंड में संस्कृत अध्ययन और Indology की समृद्ध परंपरा है।
क्राकोव शहर में हमने Indian Studies Chair की स्थापना की है। आज हमने कल्चर और एजुकेशन, और साथ-साथ स्पोर्ट्स और टुरिज़म में भी सहयोग को और सुदृढ़ करने का निर्णय लिया है।
Friends,
आज हमने regional और global developments पर भी विस्तार से चर्चा की। भारत और पोलैंड, दोनों डेमॉक्रैटिक वैल्यूस और rule of law में विश्वास रखते हैं। हमारा मानना है कि global governance institutions को अधिक सशक्त और प्रभावी बनाने के लिए रिफॉर्म आवश्यक है।

title: 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum to be Held in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan on 26–27 October 2026: Lok Sabha Speaker
subtitle:
The Prime Minister of India will grace the forum and meet the leaders of visiting delegations: Lok Sabha Speaker

Presiding Officers of Parliaments, Members of Parliament and other dignitaries from BRICS member and partner countries to deliberate on strategic priorities for parliaments: Lok Sabha Speaker

Global parliamentary leaders to assemble in New Delhi for the conference being hosted under India's chairship on the theme of people-centric development: Lok Sabha Speaker

Deliberations to cover parliamentary functioning in relation to institutional resilience, ethical AI and digital transformation, global governance reforms and sustainable development: Lok Sabha Speaker

International Affairs Committees of BRICS member and partner countries to discuss parliamentary diplomacy, capacity building and the exchange of best practices: Lok Sabha Speaker
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 4:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Parliament of India will host the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum on 26 and 27 October 2026 in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan. The conference will be inaugurated on 26 October.
Addressing a press conference at Parliament House today, Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla said that the conference marks a new chapter in the history of India's parliamentary diplomacy. It will bring together Presiding Officers and parliamentary leaders from BRICS member and partner countries, Union Ministers, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha Shri Harivansh, Presiding Officers of State Legislatures, Members of Parliament and other dignitaries.
The Lok Sabha Speaker stated that the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi would grace the event and meet the leaders of the visiting delegations.
He further stated that the conference would feature bilateral and multilateral interactions with the leaders of visiting delegations and parliamentary friendship groups. A meeting of the Secretaries of the delegations will be held on 25 October 2026 to finalise the Joint Statement of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum.
Highlighting the central theme of the programme, he said that the Forum would deliberate on the overarching theme of “Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development.”
He added that, building on the legacy of the BRICS Parliamentary Forum, the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum would facilitate consensus-based dialogue through the following four high-level sessions:
(i) Resilience: The critical role of parliaments in strengthening institutions to ensure a better future.
(ii) Innovation: Promoting human-centred innovation in artificial intelligence and digital technologies through parliaments.
(iii) Cooperation: Ensuring a more representative system of global governance through parliamentary cooperation.
(iv) Sustainability: The role of parliaments in ensuring a sustainable and inclusive future for our countries.
In addition, a special meeting of the Chairpersons of the International Affairs Committees of the parliaments of BRICS member and partner countries will be held to deliberate on parliamentary diplomacy, capacity building and the exchange of best practices.
Shri Birla further stated that, alongside high-level plenary sessions, parallel meetings and bilateral exchanges, the conference would also feature a cultural programme. The Vice-President of India will host a banquet in honour of the distinguished guests.
Members of the delegations will visit the Parliament of India and also enjoy cultural visits in Delhi. The conference will conclude on 27 October.
भारत की संसद द्वारा 26 और 27 अक्टूबर 2026 को आयोजित होने जा रहे 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum से पूर्व आज संसद परिसर, नई दिल्ली में प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेंस को संबोधित किया।

इस ऐतिहासिक सम्मेलन में ब्रिक्स के 11 Member Countries तथा 10 Partner Countries की संसदों के पीठासीन अधिकारी और संसदीय शिष्टमंडल भाग लेंगे। इस अवसर पर माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी की गरिमामयी उपस्थिति रहेगी। प्रधानमंत्री जी कार्यक्रम में सहभागिता करेंगे तथा आगंतुक अतिथियों के साथ संवाद करेंगे।

12वें ब्रिक्स संसदीय फोरम का मुख्य विषय “Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development” है। इसके अंतर्गत Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability जैसे महत्वपूर्ण विषयों पर विचार-विमर्श होगा। सम्मेलन में ब्रिक्स सदस्य एवं भागीदार देशों की अंतरराष्ट्रीय मामलों संबंधी संसदीय समितियों के अध्यक्षों की विशेष बैठक, द्विपक्षीय एवं बहुपक्षीय संवाद तथा विभिन्न देशों के साथ गठित Parliamentary Friendship Groups की बैठकें भी आयोजित की जाएँगी।

माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व में सितंबर 2026 में आयोजित ब्रिक्स शिखर सम्मेलन सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न हुआ, जिसमें सभी सदस्य देशों ने भाग लिया और महत्वपूर्ण घोषणाएँ की गईं। 12वाँ ब्रिक्स संसदीय फोरम इसी दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम है, जो विभिन्न देशों के बीच संसदीय सहयोग को सुदृढ़ करने और साझा वैश्विक चुनौतियों के समाधान हेतु संवाद को आगे बढ़ाएगा।

title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Interacts with Farmers at Kisan Chaupal in Haryana’s Karnal, Calls for Balanced Fertiliser Use and Natural Farming
subtitle:
“I am a servant of farmers and will never allow their dignity or the honour of farming to be compromised”: Union Agriculture Minister

Farmers should follow Soil Health Cards instead of imitating others when applying fertilisers: Shri Chouhan

Natural farming can be profitable when practised correctly; minister shares experience from his own farm

Shri Chouhan praises Haryana farmers for improved stubble management and adoption of Super Seeder technology to curb pollution

Balanced nutrition, natural farming and improved animal husbandry are key to the future of farmers: Shri Chouhan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 9:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today formally launched the nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from the historic town of Taraori in Haryana’s Karnal district. During an interactive Kisan Chaupal organised as part of the campaign, he engaged directly with farmers and stressed that serving the farming community was his highest duty. Shri Chouhan reiterated that, under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, protecting the dignity, honour and self-respect of farmers and farming remained a top priority for the Central Government. Haryana Agriculture Minister Shri Shyam Singh Rana, local legislators, senior agricultural scientists from the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI), and a large number of progressive farmers attended the programme.
Opening the interaction, Shri Chouhan said he regarded himself not as a leader holding a high office but as a servant of farmers and a committed farmer himself. “This turban symbolises the honour and self-respect of farmers, and I will never allow it to be lowered. The need of the hour is to bring modern practices and traditional wisdom together in a way that protects our soil while improving farmers’ incomes,” he said.
Follow Soil Health Cards, not the herd mentality, when applying fertilisers
Expressing concern over excessive use of chemical fertilisers, Shri Chouhan clarified that the objective of the Khet Bachao Abhiyan was not to oppose fertilisers indiscriminately but to promote their balanced and scientific use. Explaining the consequences of excessive application, he said that just as taking calcium supplements without a medical need could harm the body, applying chemical fertilisers unnecessarily was damaging soil fertility. He urged farmers to move away from competitive and imitative practices in fertiliser use. “If Ramlal applies four bags of fertiliser, Shyamlal should not feel compelled to apply four and a half bags. Farmers must break free from this tendency to imitate others. First, assess the soil through the Soil Health Card and then provide balanced nutrition according to its actual requirements,” he said. Such an approach would help reduce cultivation costs while protecting soil health for future generations, he added.
Start natural farming on at least one acre and follow the prescribed methods
Addressing farmers’ concerns about natural farming, Shri Chouhan shared his personal experience of cultivating vegetables, fruits and other crops on his own farm, where he also practises natural farming. He emphasised that natural farming could deliver good results when undertaken using scientifically appropriate methods. The correct proportions and timely application of Jeevamrit, Ghanjeevamrit and Beejamrit were important to its success, he said. Shri Chouhan encouraged farmers with landholdings of three to five acres to begin by adopting natural farming on just one acre and learning the complete process before expanding it to the rest of their land. Once farmers witnessed the benefits themselves, he said, others would be encouraged to follow the practice. He stressed that natural farming should not be dismissed as an unviable proposition, adding that farmers could benefit when they adopted the practice properly.
Discussion on indigenous cattle and sex-sorted semen technology
Farmers raised questions during the Chaupal about the conservation of indigenous cattle breeds, the market value of their milk and advanced breeding technologies that increase the likelihood of producing female calves through sex-sorted semen. The issues were discussed in the presence of agricultural scientists. It was conveyed that the government was working to validate such technologies more widely and make them accessible to farmers at affordable rates. The discussion also highlighted the need to secure better market prices for milk from indigenous cows and the role of cow dung and cow urine in natural farming.
Shri Chouhan praises Haryana farmers for stubble management
Shri Chouhan praised Haryana’s farmers for their increased awareness of crop residue management and the reported sharp decline in stubble-burning incidents in the state this year. Recalling the smog and smoke that often characterised this period in previous years, he said farmers in Haryana had demonstrated how the adoption of crop residue management practices and technologies such as Super Seeders could help protect the environment. He described the efforts as an example for the rest of the country, crediting the collective commitment of farmers, the public and the government for the progress.
​
Kisan Chaupal focuses on practical solutions from the field
The Kisan Chaupal at Taraori served as a platform for farmers to raise issues arising from their day-to-day agricultural practices and discuss scientific solutions directly with the minister and agricultural experts. Shri Chouhan assured farmers that the Agriculture Ministry would act on their suggestions and requirements and take concrete steps to address their concerns. The interaction reinforced the campaign’s focus on balanced fertiliser use, natural farming, improved animal husbandry and sustainable agricultural practices to protect soil health and strengthen farmers’ livelihoods.

title: “Save both people and fields”: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan launches nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from Taraori in Karnal
subtitle:
“Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi feels deeply concerned about why our land and fields cannot remain healthy; protecting soil from becoming barren is our national duty”: Shri Shivraj Singh

Major rural development gift for Haryana: Permanent houses worth ₹1,343 crore approved for 28,422 poor families; Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh hands over the approval letter

“Nationwide campaign to run from 22 October to 30 November: Scientists will visit villages across the country to raise public awareness,” says Shri Shivraj Singh

“Chemical fertilisers and pesticides are turning the human body into a breeding ground for diseases: Farmers should check Soil Health Cards before applying fertilisers and adopt balanced nutrient management,” says Shri Shivraj Singh

“Hardworking farmers of Haryana have shown a new path to the entire country: They are also transforming agriculture in Madhya Pradesh,” says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

“Green ammonia will make India self-reliant in fertiliser production: Adopt crop rotation and do not kill beneficial insects and earthworms by burning crop residue,” says Shri Shivraj Singh

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today formally launched the nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from the historic town of Taraori in Karnal district, Haryana. Addressing millions of farmers, agricultural scientists and officials who joined virtually from Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and agricultural institutions across the country, Shri Chouhan warned that unless the unbalanced use of chemical fertilisers and pesticides was brought under control, the earth could eventually refuse to produce crops and the human body could become a breeding ground for diseases. On the occasion, he called for a comprehensive public awareness campaign in every village across the country from 22nd October to 30th November 2026. As Rural Development Minister, he also announced a major benefit for poor families in Haryana. He handed over to Haryana Agriculture Minister Shri Shyam Singh Rana, on behalf of the state government, an approval letter for financial assistance of ₹1,343.06 crore to construct 28,422 permanent houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Gramin.
Haryana’s farmers have shown the way forward for the entire country
Addressing a large farmers’ convention held on the historic land of Taraori, Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that Haryana’s farmers were remarkable for their hard work, dedication and willingness to experiment with new approaches. He observed that progressive farmers from Haryana were writing a new chapter of agricultural transformation not only in their own state but also in states such as Madhya Pradesh, where they were promoting modern and natural farming practices. Emphasising Haryana’s influence on agricultural progress across the country, he said that when Haryana showed the way, the entire nation moved forward in that direction. He added that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, too, felt deeply concerned about the deteriorating health of Mother Earth and the need to improve the condition of the country’s agricultural land.
Major benefit for Haryana under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana
During the programme, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, in his capacity as Union Rural Development Minister, made a major announcement for rural poor families in Haryana. He said that the central government had approved the construction of 28,422 permanent houses for eligible poor families in the state under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana. An amount of ₹1,343 crore and ₹6 lakh had been sanctioned for this purpose. Shri Chouhan handed over the formal approval letter for this significant allocation to Haryana Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Minister Shri Shyam Singh Rana, who was present on the stage. The approval is expected to help thousands of economically disadvantaged families in the state realise their dream of owning a permanent home.
Affordable fertilisers do not mean indiscriminate use; the government is bearing the subsidy burden
Speaking about fertiliser prices and the government’s commitment to farmers, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that despite rising prices in international markets, the central government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, was ensuring that farmers did not face any additional financial burden. The government was bearing a substantial fertiliser subsidy of more than ₹1.5 lakh crore to ensure that farmers could continue to obtain a bag of urea for just ₹266 and a bag of DAP for ₹1,350. However, he cautioned farmers against assuming that the availability of affordable fertilisers justified their excessive use. “Getting fertilisers at affordable prices certainly does not mean that we should keep applying four bags of urea to our fields. It is a misconception that applying more fertiliser will produce a bigger harvest. Applying fertilisers without need is like wasting our hard-earned money and poisoning the soil. Just as a person can become ill by taking medicines without being sick, excessive fertiliser use is making the health of our Mother Earth deteriorate,” he said. He added that India was now moving towards the use of green ammonia, which would help the country become fully self-reliant (
atmanirbhar
) in fertiliser production in the future.
Pesticides are turning the human body into a breeding ground for diseases; both people and fields must be protected
Highlighting the serious consequences of chemical-intensive farming, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that consuming food produced with poisonous pesticides and excessive, uncontrolled fertiliser use was increasingly turning the human body into a breeding ground for serious diseases. He observed that air, water and food were essential for human survival, and that ancient scriptures regarded food as Brahma, or the divine. If the food itself became impure, he warned, the very existence of human civilisation could be threatened. He stressed that the present effort was not merely a struggle to protect soil but a sacred mission to safeguard both agricultural land and human life. Protecting the health of the fields, he emphasised, was inseparable from protecting the health of the people who depended on them.
Three practical principles for soil conservation
Union Minister Shri Chouhan outlined three key measures that farmers could adopt to preserve soil fertility and maintain productive agricultural land.
Balanced fertiliser use based on Soil Health Cards
: Farmers should check their Soil Health Cards on their mobile phones and identify which nutrients are deficient in their soil. They should then apply only the required fertilisers, in balanced quantities, to address those deficiencies rather than using fertilisers indiscriminately.
Changing the crop cycle through crop rotation
: Instead of repeatedly growing paddy followed by wheat, farmers should introduce pulses such as chickpea, lentil and pigeon pea into their cropping cycles. The roots of pulse crops naturally fix nitrogen in the soil, helping to improve its fertility and replenish nutrients.
Adopting natural farming on at least half an acre
: Farmers need not initially convert their entire landholding to natural farming. Even if they have five acres, they should begin by adopting natural farming on at least half an acre. They can prepare Beejamrit and Ghanjeevamrit using cow dung, cow urine and soil collected from beneath trees. This would provide chemical-free food for household consumption, reduce cultivation costs and improve soil health. Over two to three years, soil conditions would improve and production could reach levels comparable to those achieved through conventional farming.
Crop-residue management and protection of earthworms, the soil’s natural allies
Appreciating the efforts of Taraori’s farmers to manage crop residue and maintain high levels of organic carbon in their soil, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that burning crop residue was a self-destructive practice. He explained that setting fire to fields not only causes air pollution but also destroys trillions of microorganisms living in the upper and lower layers of the soil, along with beneficial insects and earthworms that help produce natural manure. These organisms play an essential role in maintaining the soil’s natural fertility. Protecting earthworms and beneficial insects, he stressed, was therefore crucial to preserving the health and productivity of agricultural land.
Nationwide public awareness campaign to run from 22nd October to 30th November, 2026
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan called upon vice-chancellors of agricultural universities, the Director General of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), scientists and officials to leave their laboratories and offices and visit villages across the country from 22nd October to 30th November, 2026. They should organise village-level meetings and discussions with farmers to explain the importance of soil health and balanced farming practices. He expressed his resolve to remain actively involved in the campaign on the ground himself, ensuring that the initiative reached farmers directly and helped protect India’s agricultural land from becoming barren.
Farmers raise their hands and pledge to protect their fields
At the conclusion of his address, responding to Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s appeal, the farmers gathered at the venue raised both hands, clenched their fists and took a collective pledge amid resounding slogans of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai”. They resolved to use chemicals in their fields in a balanced manner, change their crop cycles, refrain from burning crop residue and gradually adopt natural farming practices to protect the health of Mother Earth.
The historic launch was attended by several prominent agricultural scientists and administrative officials, including ICAR Director General and Secretary of the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) Dr Mangi Lal Jat and Haryana Additional Chief Secretary (Agriculture) Shri Vijendra Kumar, along with a large number of farmers. During the programme, the dignitaries also released a booklet on the ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’.

title: Secretary DARE Calls for Reimagining Agricultural Higher Education Through Global Partnerships
subtitle: Addressing Indian agricultural diaspora at the World Food Prize Foundation programme in the United States virtually, Dr Jat highlights industry–academia collaboration, policy dialogue and international knowledge exchange
date:
