content:
Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), has called for reimagining agricultural higher education to prepare future professionals to address global challenges, including climate change, natural resource degradation, biodiversity loss and the growing demand for nutritious and healthy food.
Addressing a Roundtable organized on the sidelines of the '2026 Norman E Borlaug International Dialogue' during the World Food Prize Foundation at Des Moines in the United States virtually, Dr. Jat delivered his remarks as President of the National Academy of Agricultural Sciences (NAAS), India. He acknowledged the Academy’s representation at the programme by its Secretary, Dr. B.S. Dwivedi; Foreign Secretary, Dr. Karim Meredia; and Convener of the International Chapter for the Western Hemisphere, Dr. P.V. Varaprasad.
In his address, Dr Jat emphasised the need to transform agricultural education and research to meet the evolving requirements of agri-food systems. He highlighted India’s long-standing partnerships with global institutions, noting that international collaboration enables mutual learning and provides opportunities to share scientific and educational advancements.
He stressed the importance of moving beyond production-centric agriculture towards an integrated agri-food systems and value-chain approach. He underscored the need for stronger collaboration between academia and industry to develop industry-ready human resources and facilitate industry participation across the agri-food value chain, including support for farmers.
Highlighting the role of NAAS in agricultural policy and research, Dr Jat noted the importance of policy dialogues, policy papers and policy briefs in addressing critical issues in agricultural research and development. He emphasised the need to bring together researchers, policymakers, academic institutions, industry and other stakeholders to develop collaborative solutions to emerging challenges.
Dr Jat also highlighted efforts to connect the Indian agricultural diaspora with domestic research and educational institutions. Strengthening these networks, he noted, can facilitate international knowledge exchange and contribute to reimagining agricultural higher education through global expertise and experience.
Referring to efforts to expand international institutional partnerships, Dr Jat highlighted the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Council for Agricultural Science and Technology (CAST). The partnership is expected to create new avenues for cooperation in agricultural research, capacity development and knowledge exchange.
Dr. Jat expressed confidence that stronger international partnerships would contribute to advancing agricultural research, education and extension, with particular relevance for countries of the Global South. He called for collective efforts to transform agri-food systems and build a more resilient and sustainable future for agriculture worldwide.

title: IICA signs MoU with Association of ARCs in India to strengthen industry linkages with its flagship programme

content:
The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, recently signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Association of ARCs in India. The Association is the representative body of Asset Reconstruction Companies registered with the Reserve Bank of India. The MoU was signed under the august presence of Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh. Director General & CEO, IICA, by Shri Amrinder Puri, Chief Administrative Officer, IICA and Shri Hari Hara Mishra, Chief Executive Officer, Association of ARCs in India.
The MoU aims to deepen industry linkages of the Post Graduate Insolvency Programme (PGIP), run by IICA’s Centre for Insolvency and Bankruptcy. The PGIP develops a skilled cadre of Insolvency Professionals and Turnaround Specialists. The MoU captures the strategic alignment as decided in the meeting convened by Ministry of Corporate Affairs on 2nd  September 2026.
Delivering the keynote address on the occasion, Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, DG &CEO IICA informed the role of Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs) in the insolvency resolution ecosystem, including their eligibility and participation as resolution applicants under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). He highlighted that the significant development in the evolution of ARCs came on 11 October 2022, when the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), following the recommendations of the Sudarshan Sen Committee, issued its regulatory framework titled
Review of Regulatory Framework for Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs)
(RBI/2022-23/128). The framework permitted eligible ARCs to act as resolution applicants under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC), subject to the prescribed regulatory conditions.
This development expanded the potential role of ARCs in corporate insolvency resolution, enabling them to participate in resolution processes and contribute their expertise in asset valuation, debt restructuring and the management of stressed assets. It also underscored the importance of transparency, operational efficiency and effective value realisation in the resolution of distressed businesses.
Speaking on behalf ARCs, Shri Hari Hara Mishra, CEO ARC India mentioned that this is an emerging partnership with extraordinary potential. As distressed market evolves, a repository of talent pool and research insights are critical for value maximisation for all stakeholders in the ecosystem. He desired that implementation strategy should be immediately put in place in achieving the overall objectives in general and transforming the academic rigour of PGIP course in particular.
The proposed collaboration is expected to strengthen the integration of theoretical knowledge with practical industry experience, preparing PGIP participants to respond more effectively to the complexities of insolvency resolution, corporate restructuring and financial distress management. The MoU establishes a collaborative framework built around three key pillars:
1. Industry-oriented curriculum and capacity building:
Industry experts from ARCs will contribute to teaching, faculty support to reorient PGIP course modules more industry-oriented and responsive to emerging professional requirements.
2. Research, data sharing and knowledge creation:
The collaboration will promote joint research projects in areas such as debt restructuring, financial markets, stressed assets and insolvency resolution. Data sharing, subject to applicable legal, regulatory, confidentiality and access requirements, will support evidence-based research and the development of research resources on market trends and developments.
3. Joint programmes and industry engagement:
The two institutions will explore internships, placement- related opportunities and greater industry interaction for PGIP participants. An annual joint conference will provide a platform for discussing emerging challenges, sharing professional insights and disseminating research findings.
Looking Ahead
The MoU, signed for a period of five years, provides a structured framework for sustained engagement between IICA and the Association of ARCs. The institutions will work towards translating the agreement into tangible outcomes through defined implementation strategies, collaborative research, expert-led teaching and regular review of progress.
The discussions also explored the possibility of organising a joint conference in February 2027 around the milestones of
IBC@10 and SARFAESI@25
, with the theme and programme to be finalised jointly within the broad spectrum of activities enunciated in the MoU.

content:
Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi, today launched the registration portal for the fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam (KTS 5.0) scheduled to be held from 28 November to 12 December 2026. The programme will celebrate, reaffirm and strengthen the age-old civilizational bonds between Tamil Nadu and Kashi, the two ancient seats of learning, strengthening the spirit of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat.
Speaking at the Launch, Shri Pralhad Joshi said that since ancient times, the country has had a strong cultural unity. He noted that many people visited Kashi and Rameswaram as part of their religious traditions, reflecting the deep-rooted cultural bonds between the northern and southern parts of India. He stated that the Programme would bring together students, teachers, writers, professionals, agriculturalists, artists, women and spiritual scholars. He also highlighted that educational outreach initiatives would be carried out in higher education institutions to familiarise students with the objectives of Kashi Tamil Sangamam. The Union Minister reiterated that Kashi Tamil Sangamam played an important role in strengthening national unity and celebrating India’s shared civilisational heritage.
The first Kashi Tamil Sangamam was held in 2022 and over the last four editions, it facilitated meaningful exchanges of knowledge, language, traditions and lived experiences between the two regions. The Event is organized by the Department of Higher Education, Union Ministry of Education, in collaboration with IIT Madras; Banaras Hindu University (BHU); Central Institute of Classical Tamil (CICT), Chennai; Uttar Pradesh Government and Central Govt Departments/Ministries of Culture, Railways, School Education, Tourism, Textiles, Food Processing Industries, Information & Broadcasting, Skill Development & Entrepreneurship, etc.
Theme for 2026: “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen”
The theme of KTS 5.0 is “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen”. The fifth edition seeks to bring the timeless ethical and moral wisdom of the classical Tamil text
Thirukkural
closer to the youth and learners across the country. Through educational engagement, multilingual resources and wider public outreach, the programme seeks to encourage reading, understanding and application of  universal values as enshrined in the text, in everyday life.
Participation and Itinerary
As part of the Programme, around 1,400 participants from Tamil Nadu, organized into seven groups of around 200 persons each, will undertake an eight-day journey comprising four days of travel and four days of visits and structured programmes. The itinerary will include Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya, featuring cultural, academic, domain-specific and spiritual engagements. The emphasis on youth participation will enable a new generation to engage meaningfully with India’s classical knowledge traditions and carry their values into contemporary academic, professional and social life.
Registration Details
Interested applicants may register through the official portal at
https://kashitamil.iitm.ac.in/
hosted by IIT Madras with effect from October 22, 2026. The Portal will accept applications till November 13, 2026 under seven categories: (i) Students, (ii) Teachers, (iii) Writers and Media Professionals, (iv) Agriculture and Allied Sectors, (v) Professionals and Artisans, (vi) Women and (vii) Spiritual leaders.
Major Initiatives under KTS 5.0
A nationwide Students’ Engagement Programme will be undertaken through 1,000 Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) across the country to promote wider understanding of the
Thirukkural
among students from diverse academic disciplines and linguistic backgrounds. The Initiative will include structured study, research and campus-based activities for wider dissemination of  the teachings and values of the
Thirukkural
. The details are available on the portal
www.kts.cict.in
of the Central Institute of Classical Tamil, Chennai.
Thirukkural
experts from Tamil Nadu will visit various schools and colleges in Varanasi and introduce the students to the core values of the Text through orientation modules, interactive sessions, quiz etc. The National Book Trust in association with the Rashtriya e-Pustakalaya will conduct interactive sessions in schools in Varanasi on reading habits, story telling and creative activities
KTS 5.0 will also leverage technology to make the teachings of the
Thirukkural
accessible to a wider audience across India.
The Ministry of Education invites eligible applicants from Tamil Nadu, especially youth and students, to register for Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 and participate in this celebration of India’s cultural oneness, linguistic diversity and shared civilisational inheritance.

title: CAQM Reviews Air Pollution Control Measures in Punjab and Haryana, Calls for Prompt Ground-Level Action
subtitle: Focus on prevention of Paddy Stubble Burning, effective utilization of CRM Machinery, stronger Enforcement and control of other key Pollution Sources
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 7:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), under the Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM, held separate review meetings with the Governments of Punjab and Haryana in Chandigarh today to review the measures being undertaken for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning and abatement of other key sources of air pollution, calling for prompt action(s) on the ground.
The meeting with the Government of Punjab focused on implementation of the State Action Plan for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning in accordance with CAQM Direction No. 99 dated 15.05.2026. The Commission reviewed on-ground enforcement measures, District-level preparedness and monitoring mechanisms in place for effective paddy stubble management.
The availability, deployment and effective utilization of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery at the District and farmer levels were reviewed, along with the identification of gaps in machinery utilization and arrangements for the collection, transportation and utilization of paddy straw through
in-situ
and
ex-situ
management. The Commission emphasized the need to strengthen the crop-residue supply chain and ensure effective utilization of available machinery during the peak harvesting period.
The meeting also covered field validation of burnt-area assessment through satellite-based fire alerts, along with District-wise deployment of drones and low-cost sensors for monitoring stubble-burning incidents. Compliance with CAQM Direction No. 92, mandating the use of paddy straw-based biomass pellets/ briquettes in brick kilns, and progress towards prescribed targets for biomass co-firing in thermal power plants were also reviewed.
The meeting with the Government of Haryana covered a broader range of air pollution sources, including paddy stubble burning, abatement of vehicular pollution, dust from roads and open areas, dust from construction and demolition (C&D) activities and industrial pollution, along with other identified sectoral measures.
With regard to paddy stubble burning, the Commission reviewed implementation of the State Action Plan, including on-ground enforcement, deployment and utilization of CRM machinery, crop-residue supply-chain management, field validation of burnt-area assessment and the use of drones and low-cost sensors for monitoring burning incidents. Compliance with Direction No. 92 regarding biomass pellets/ briquettes in brick kilns and progress on biomass co-firing in thermal power plants were also taken up.
The review of vehicular pollution covered installation of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system at fuel and CNG stations for enforcement of requirements relating to valid Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCCs), action against end-of-life vehicles, adoption of cleaner mobility measures and progress towards phasing out diesel-operated auto rickshaws in NCR Districts.
Measures for dust mitigation from roads and open areas, including road-dust control and mechanized road sweeping, were also reviewed. The Commission further examined measures for controlling dust emissions from C&D activities and implementation of prescribed dust-mitigation measures. The review also covered industrial pollution control, including compliance with applicable norms and monitoring and enforcement measures relating to industrial units and other identified sources.
The Commission emphasized the need for time-bound implementation of State Action Plans, its enforcement and continuous field-level monitoring, supported by close coordination among the concerned State Departments, District Administrations and enforcement agencies. The States were advised to address implementation gaps on priority and ensure timely corrective action across the respective sectors. The Commission emphasized on greater facilitation of farmers with
in-situ
crop residue management machinery and strengthened
ex-situ
mechanism. State Governments of Haryana and Punjab were also advised to implement IEC Action Plans on-ground more effectively.
The Commission emphasized that paddy stubble management should be pursued not merely as a measure to prevent burning, but as an opportunity to improve the well-being of citizens while fostering a robust industrial ecosystem of a circular economy, with greater utilization of paddy straw as a resource. The Commission called for prompt action at the ground level and further cautioned the District Administrations that any laxity that leads to rise in stubble-burning incidents shall be viewed seriously.
CAQM reiterated that sustained and coordinated efforts by the State Governments and all concerned agencies are essential for effective prevention of paddy stubble burning and comprehensive abatement of air pollution, particularly during the critical winter period.

In his address, Shri Yadav said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Union Government had progressively strengthened the legal framework governing waste management by introducing sector-specific rules for nine waste streams: plastic waste, battery waste, e-waste, waste tyres, used oil, end-of-life vehicles, construction and demolition waste, non-ferrous scrap metal and solid waste. These rules focused on waste prevention, recycling, reuse, remanufacturing and resource recovery across the product lifecycle. The Minister also highlighted that as on date, nearly 499.60 lakh metric tonnes of waste had been processed across regulated waste streams, with more than 86,043 producers and 4,880 recyclers registered under Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) frameworks.
Highlighting the role of EPR, the Minister said that the framework requires producers, importers and brand owners to ensure environmentally sound management of products at the end of their life. The transfer of EPR certificates provided financial incentives to recyclers, encouraging capacity expansion, technological advancement and increased recycling, while contributing to job creation and livelihoods across the recycling value chain. Shri Yadav emphasised that regulation alone could not create a circular economy and highlighted the importance of Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE) initiative, which calls for mindful and deliberate resource utilisation instead of destructive consumption.
On Industry concerns regarding digital compliance, EPR market operations and transaction timelines, Shri Yadav invited stakeholders to continue sharing practical problems and suggestions. He said the Government is working on a market-based approach and urged industry representatives to engage openly to resolve outstanding issues. On plastic waste management, the Minister called for greater coordination between producers and recyclers to address concerns over the availability of recyclable material and recycling capacity. He said the objective went beyond issuing certificates to creating jobs, strengthening local industry capacity, promoting knowledge-sharing and advancing technology.
While talking about Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, Shri Yadav stressed the need for technology adoption, capacity building, online monitoring, stronger accountability and financial sustainability of urban local bodies. The Minister also highlighted the importance of four-stream segregation of solid waste – wet, dry, sanitary and special-care waste – and public participation. Shri Yadav concluded by emphasising that effective implementation of the SWM Rules would help control legacy waste and strengthen urban systems. He called for coordinated efforts by the government, industry and urban local bodies to advance the circular economy. He further called for stronger recovery of critical minerals from e-waste and batteries, and greater industry participation in developing secondary raw-material markets and strengthening supply-chain traceability.

The Department of Fisheries, Government of Madhya Pradesh and the Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying (MoFAHD), Government of India (GoI) are
organising Fisheries Investors & Exporters Conclave 2026 to
be held on 23 October 2026 in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. The Conclave aims to strengthen linkages between inland fisheries production and investment, processing, cold-chain infrastructure, value addition and export markets. It seeks to encourage a shift from a predominantly production-oriented approach towards an integrated value-chain model, with a focus on improving market access and returns for fishermen and fish farmers.
The Conclave will bring together investors, exporters, fishers, more than 1,000 fish farmers from various parts of Madhya Pradesh, fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs), entrepreneurs, start-ups, processors, financial institutions, research organisations and other stakeholders. Deliberations will focus on enterprise development, access to finance, market linkages and opportunities for collaboration across the inland fisheries value chain, with particular emphasis on integrating inland States into the fisheries investment and export ecosystem.
A key feature of the Conclave will be the release of the MADHYA PRADESH FISHERIES INVESTMENT AND EXPORT GUIDELINES, 2026. Madhya Pradesh has been notified by the Center as a Reservoir Fisheries Cluster.  The policy is intended to facilitate investment across key segments of the fisheries value chain, including hatcheries, fish seed and feed, reservoir and cage fisheries, aquatic animal health, processing, cold-chain infrastructure, logistics, value addition and market development.
The programme will also feature the release of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) on the export potential of inland States, the virtual inauguration of Integrated Cage Culture Units.  During the event, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj will hand over the Administrative Approval for the Integrated Development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars in Madhya Pradesh. These initiatives are expected to support investment in inland fisheries, promote the productive utilisation of water resources and encourage enterprise development.
The Conclave assumes significance in the context of India's expanding fisheries sector and its growing contribution to food security, livelihoods and export earnings. India’s fish production reached 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024–25, of which 151.60 lakh tonnes came from inland fisheries, accounting for nearly three-fourths of the country's total fish production. India's seafood exports were valued at ₹73,890 crore in 2025–26. These figures highlight the importance of strengthening infrastructure, processing capabilities and market linkages to realise the potential of inland fisheries.
Madhya Pradesh, with nearly 4.50 lakh hectares of water area, offers considerable potential for inland fisheries development. The Conclave seeks to connect the State's production base, along with that of other inland States, with investment, processing, value addition and domestic and export markets.
The Conclave will be graced by Dr. Mohan Yadav, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh; Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj; and Shri Narayan Singh Pawar, Hon’ble Minister, Department of Fisherman Welfare and Fisheries Development, Government of Madhya Pradesh.
Through stakeholder engagement and deliberations on investment and market development, the Conclave seeks to promote more competitive and market-oriented inland fisheries value chains, expand opportunities for enterprises and exporters, and strengthen livelihood and income opportunities for fishermen and fish farmers.

title: SAEINDIA to Host APAC 23 in New Delhi, Bringing AsiaPacific’s Mobility Engineering Community Together
subtitle: 23rd Edition of Asia Pacific Automotive Engineering Conference 2026 to convene 1,000+ delegates, 500+ mobility experts and industry leaders from across the region from 13–14 November 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 3:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
SAEINDIA is set to host APAC 23 – 23rd Asia Pacific Automotive Engineering Conference 2026, one of the region’s prominent forums for automotive and mobility engineering, from 13–14 November 2026 at Yashobhoomi Convention Centre, New Delhi.
Organised under the theme “Xellerating towards Safe, Secure, Sustainable & Intelligent Mobility,” APAC 23 will bring together mobility leaders, engineers, technologists, researchers, policymakers, academia, start-ups and solution providers from India and across the Asia-Pacific region to exchange ideas, showcase emerging technologies and explore the future of mobility.
The conference assumes special significance for India as SAEINDIA hosts APAC for the second time after a gap of 15 years, placing the country at the centre of an influential regional dialogue on the technologies and engineering solutions shaping the next generation of transportation.
A Legacy of Collaboration Across Asia-Pacific
Originating in 1981 as the International Pacific Conference, APAC has evolved into a collaborative automotive engineering forum representing 11 countries across the AsiaPacific region. Over the decades, it has created a platform for engineering communities to exchange knowledge, strengthen international collaboration and address emerging challenges across the automotive and mobility ecosystem.
As the global mobility sector undergoes rapid transformation driven by electrification, software, artificial intelligence, connectivity, automation, sustainability and evolving safety requirements, APAC 23 will provide a timely platform to examine how engineering innovation can translate these developments into safe, secure and sustainable mobility solutions.
Bringing the Mobility Ecosystem Under One Roof
APAC 23 is expected to welcome 1,000+ delegates and 500+ mobility experts, with participation from leading automotive OEMs, component manufacturers, technology companies, engineering service providers, research organisations, academic institutions, start-ups and government and regulatory stakeholders.
The two-day conference is expected to feature 150+ technical presentations and 80+ exhibitors, creating an extensive platform for knowledge exchange, technology demonstration, business networking and cross-border collaboration.
Technical discussions at APAC 23 will span some of the most important areas influencing the future of mobility, including:
Future Powertrains
Automated, Connected,
Safe & Smart Mobility
Cybersecurity & Artificial Intelligence
Software-Defined Vehicles and Vehicle as a Digital Platform
Digital Transformation & Digital Twins
Vehicle Dynamics  Human Factors
Advanced Materials & Lightweighting
Energy, Emissions & Life Cycle Assessment  Standards & Regulations
Beyond a Conference: An Integrated Mobility Platform
APAC 23 has been designed as more than a conventional technical conference. Alongside plenary and technical sessions, the event will feature an Exposition, TechHive, Technology Theatre and dedicated networking and business engagement opportunities, enabling participants to experience mobility innovation from multiple perspectives.
The APAC 23 Exposition will provide organisations with a platform to demonstrate technologies, products, engineering capabilities and next-generation mobility solutions to a highly relevant audience of industry professionals and decision-makers.
The Technology Theatre, located within the exposition area, will offer an interactive platform for organisations to present new technologies, solutions, product innovations and engineering developments directly to conference participants.
TechHive: Giving Mobility Start-ups a Global Stage
A major highlight of APAC 23 will be TechHive, a dedicated platform created to connect mobility start-ups with the wider automotive ecosystem.
TechHive will provide emerging companies with opportunities to showcase innovations, interact with industry leaders, technology experts, investors, potential customers and collaborators, and build visibility within the Asia-Pacific mobility community.
Through TechHive, APAC 23 aims to strengthen the connection between emerging innovation and established industry, encouraging collaborations capable of accelerating new mobility technologies from concept to real-world application.
India at the Centre of the Mobility Transformation India is rapidly emerging as one of the world’s most significant mobility markets and engineering hubs. The convergence of a large automotive manufacturing ecosystem, strong engineering talent, an expanding start-up landscape and increasing investments in electric, connected, software-defined and sustainable mobility presents a unique opportunity for the country. By bringing APAC back to India after 15 years, SAEINDIA aims to facilitate deeper engagement between India and the wider Asia-Pacific automotive engineering community and create new opportunities for technology exchange, research collaboration, partnerships and business development.
Opportunities for Industry Participation
With the conference approaching, SAEINDIA is inviting organisations and professionals across the mobility ecosystem to participate in APAC 23 through delegate registrations, sponsorship, exposition and TechHive.
The conference offers organisations an opportunity to position their technologies and capabilities before a focused audience, engage with mobility decision-makers and engineering professionals, develop new partnerships and contribute to conversations defining the future direction of mobility in the Asia-Pacific region.
APAC 23 – Asia Pacific Automotive Engineering Conference 2026
Dates: 13–14 November 2026 Venue: Yashobhoomi Convention Centre, New Delhi, India
Theme: “Xellerating towards Safe, Secure, Sustainable & Intelligent Mobility”
About SAEINDIA
SAEINDIA is a leading professional engineering society dedicated to advancing mobility knowledge and solutions in India. It brings together engineers, industry professionals, researchers, academicians and students across the mobility ecosystem and facilitates technical knowledge sharing, professional development, industry-academia collaboration and engineering innovation.
Through conferences, technical programmes, professional development initiatives, student competitions and industry engagement platforms, SAEINDIA contributes to developing engineering capabilities and advancing mobility technologies in India.

content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today attended the inauguration and foundation-stone laying ceremony of projects worth ₹8,941 crore related to the rejuvenation of the Yamuna in Delhi. On this occasion, Lieutenant Governor of Delhi Shri Taranjit Singh Sandhu and Chief Minister Smt. Rekha Gupta, along with several other dignitaries, were present.
In his address, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that today the inauguration and foundation-stone laying of important projects worth nearly ₹9,000 crore for the purification of the Yamuna took place here. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, as soon as our party’s government was formed in Delhi, called a major meeting and placed his vision of purifying the Yamuna before the Delhi Government and the Ministry of Home Affairs. In such a short time, we have achieved more than 40 percent success.
Shri Amit Shah said that for the past 30 years, previous governments allowed Delhi’s sewage water to be discharged into the Yamuna and dumped 2,000 tonnes of cow dung from dairies into the Yamuna every day. At one time, governments of the main opposition party’s allies were in power in Uttar Pradesh and Haryana, and industrial waste water from Haryana as well as dirty water from Uttar Pradesh also flowed into the Yamuna. He said that today our party’s governments are in power at the Centre and in Delhi, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh. Our governments in these four states have jointly prepared time-bound roadmaps for Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Delhi, through which we will make the Yamuna clean by 2029. Shri Shah said that we want to build a Delhi where homes are beautiful, water is pure, streets are clean, there are no mountains of garbage, and the Yamuna, once cleansed, can bestow its blessings on the people from here all the way to the Sangam. He said that Prime Minister Modi has taken up this work as an unwavering resolve, and today a very large part of that resolve is being fulfilled.
Union Home Minister said that 10 projects were inaugurated and 33 projects were initiated here today. He said that through the schemes started at a total cost of ₹8,941 crore, several lakh litres of water will be purified and flow into the Yamuna. Projects related to several areas of Delhi were inaugurated here today, and the foundation stones were also laid for the upgradation of existing STPs and the installation of new STPs. A decentralised STP pumping station has also been set up here today, and work has begun to connect sewer lines to households. We are taking forward sewer rehabilitation, tapping and drainage work. The Home Minister expressed confidence that we will purify the Yamuna before May 2029.
Shri Amit Shah said that some political parties only indulge in the politics of excuses. Previous governments in Delhi used to make excuses that they did not get any help. He said that we have answers to every claim of theirs, but those answers will be given to them after their government in Punjab goes. The previous government in Delhi did nothing except seize power in the name of protests and indulge in corruption. They played politics in the name of garbage mountains, but our government has worked to bring those garbage mountains down. In two years, gardens will come up in place of these garbage mountains.
Union Home Minister said that the Rekha Gupta government in Delhi, with the help of the Modi government at the Centre, has cleared 2.17 crore metric tonnes of garbage and freed 100 acres of land from waste. The garbage mountains at Okhla and Bhalswa have been reduced by 30 to 40 metres, the one at Ghazipur has come down by 10 to 15 metres. The previous government did no work for the purification of the Yamuna. Our government has today carried out world-class works such as
Asita East, Bansera and Vasudev Ghat at Sarai Kale Khan and ITO
. We have prepared a three-year action plan to provide sewerage connections to every household in Delhi so that dirty water can be drained out, and we will also ensure that pure drinking water reaches every home.
Shri Amit Shah said that a different game is currently being played in Delhi because our governments are continuously being elected in states across the country. He said that this is causing stomachache to the opponents, which is why they are making the excuse of vote theft. Opposition parties claim that our party does not come to power through popular votes, but by stealing votes. The entire country understands — and has understood — the opposition parties and their parties. Shri Shah said that by creating a hue and cry over vote theft, the opposition parties want to save the votes of infiltrators.
Union Home Minister said that opposition parties make excuses sometimes about EVMs and sometimes about vote theft. The Home Minister said that when they claim their party’s government will remain for 30 years, the opposition parties tell the people that vote theft is taking place, otherwise how would Amit Shah have known. Shri Shah said that he was born here, lives here, and remains among the people of the country, and he does not have to go abroad every six months. He said that given the kind of negative politics the opposition is doing, the opposition’s government will never be formed for the next 30 years.
Shri Amit Shah said that recently in Kerala, elections were held with the same voter list, Election Commission and EVMs, and after winning the election the opposition took the oath and is now praising the Election Commission. When the opposition won in Telangana, the Election Commission was also good and the voter list was good too. When they won in Himachal, the Election Commission and voter list were good then as well. In Tamil Nadu, when the party they supported won the election, the Election Commission and voter list were good then too. Shri Shah said that wherever the opposition loses the election, the Election Commission is not proper there. If the courts give a judgment in favour of the opposition, the courts are good, but if they give a judgment against the opposition, the courts are not proper. Shri Shah said that these double standards of the opposition will not work, and the people have now understood all of this.
Union Home Minister said that the opposition cannot negate the people’s mandate by gathering cadres from some neighbouring states and staging protests in Delhi. He said that the people of the country are both watching and understanding the opposition. He said that from our party’s booth workers to Prime Minister Modi ji, our crores of workers live among the people, know their sorrows, and work day and night to solve their problems. If we look at the example of the Yamuna, the main opposition party and other parties’ previous governments ruled Delhi for 30 years, but they did nothing for the Yamuna. Shri Shah said that now the good fortune of cleaning the entire Yamuna, from Yamunotri to the Sangam, is going to come to our government under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The Home Minister said that the opposition cannot negate the country’s mandate through such political tactics and mobocracy. He said that if one wants to win elections, one should go among the people to understand their sufferings and pains; nothing is achieved through dharnas and protests. Wherever you have been elected, bring schemes and do work to remove the people’s sorrows, pains, sufferings and disorder; otherwise even the remaining existence will come to an end.

title: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to organise 19th Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition on 23–24 October 2026 in Bhubaneswar
subtitle:
2nd National Urban Conclave 2026 to be held on 24–25 October in Bhubaneswar

Shri Tokhan Sahu, Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, in the presence of Shri Mohan Charan Majhi to inaugurate the conclave

Urban Mobility India 2026 to focus on ‘Urban Accessibility and Liveability in Digital Age’

National Urban Conclave to deliberate on ‘Urban Rising – Rethinking Urban Systems, Solutions and Delivery’

Two major national events to bring together policymakers, urban experts and stakeholders to discuss the future of Indian cities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 6:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India, with the support of  Government of Odisha, is organising two major events in Bhubaneswar this week.
The 19th Urban Mobility India (UMI) Conference and Exhibition 2026 will be held on 23–24 October, followed by the second edition of the National Urban Conclave on 24–25 October 2026. Both events will take place at Hotel Mayfair Sanctuary, Bhubaneswar, Odisha.
Addressing a curtain-raiser press conference in Bhubaneswar today, Shri Satinder Pal Singh, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, briefed the media about the National Urban Conclave 2026. Shri Praveer Kumar, Joint Secretary, MoHUA, shared details of the Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition.
Smt. Usha Padhee, Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Odisha briefed the media on state collaboration.  Shri Yogesh Antil , Director, MoHUA, was also present on the occasion.
National Urban Conclave 2026
Speaking about the National Urban Conclave 2026, Shri Satinder Pal Singh informed that the second edition of the Conclave will be held on 24–25 October 2026. The event is being organised by MoHUA with the support of  Government of Odisha, with support from HUDCO and NBCC. The National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA) is serving as the knowledge partner and HUDCO & NBCC being the principal sponsors.
He stated that this year’s Conclave will focus on the theme
‘Urban Rising – Rethinking Urban Systems, Solutions and Delivery’
. The deliberations will focus on strengthening urban systems, institutions and implementation mechanisms to improve the functioning of Indian cities.
Shri Satinder Pal  Singh highlighted that the National Urban Conclave provides a platform for policymakers, urban administrators, technical experts, industry representatives and other stakeholders to discuss emerging urban challenges and identify practical solutions.
The Conclave will be inaugurated by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, in the presence of Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha. Shri Anurag Jain, Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog, and Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog, will also participate as Chief Guests.
The National Urban Conclave was instituted as an annual platform for discussions on the future of urban development in India. Its inaugural edition was held in New Delhi in November 2025. The first edition brought together stakeholders for deliberations across major areas of urban development.
The Conclave will focus on seven key thematic areas:
i. The session on ‘
Right to Walk
’ will address an everyday concern in our cities: how to make streets safer and more accessible through continuous footpaths, safe school zones, better pedestrian crossings and improved last-mile connectivity.
ii. Under ‘
Water, Waste and Resource Efficiency
’, the emphasis will be on moving beyond infrastructure creation to improving service efficiency, reducing water losses, promoting treated-water reuse and recovering value from waste.
iii. The session on ‘
Affordable Housing
’ will bring attention to the growing need for rental accommodation, simpler regulatory approvals, better access to land and finance, and wider adoption of affordable, climate-resilient construction technologies.
iv. Through ‘
Integrated Urban Development and Infrastructure Delivery
’, we will examine how better coordination between agencies, integrated utility planning and GIS-based systems can reduce duplication and improve the planning and execution of urban infrastructure.
v. A key question under ‘
New Paradigms for Urban Service Delivery
’ will be how municipalities can deliver better services through clearer institutional responsibilities, stronger finances, procurement reforms, technical capacity and partnerships with the private sector.
vi. The session on ‘
Model Building Bye-Laws
’ will consider how the existing regulatory framework can be revised to simplify building approvals, strengthen safety and accessibility, and respond to climate resilience and emerging construction technologies.
vii. Finally, ‘
Model Municipal Law
’ will examine the legislative reforms needed to strengthen municipal autonomy, clarify the powers of elected representatives and executive authorities, and improve institutional capacity and accountability in urban governance.
The Conclave will also include a meeting of Urban Development Ministers from states and Union Territories. This will provide an opportunity to review progress on issues discussed during earlier national and regional meetings of Urban Development Ministers, and identify priorities requiring further action and coordination.
19th Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition 2026
Briefing the media about the 19th Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition, Shri Praveer Kumar, Joint Secretary, MoHUA, informed that the two-day event will be held on 23–24 October 2026. The conference is being organised by the Ministry through the Institute of Urban Transport (India), with the support of the Government of Odisha.
He informed that the theme of this year’s conference is
‘Urban Accessibility and Liveability in Digital Age’
. The conference will focus on improving urban accessibility, integrated transport infrastructure and quality of urban life through emerging digital technologies.
Shri Kumar stated that the conference will deliberate on sustainable and low-carbon public transport, integration of different modes of transport, first- and last-mile connectivity and the role of technology in improving urban mobility. It will also examine the potential of Mobility as a Service (MaaS) and real-time GPS-based solutions in providing seamless and efficient transport services.
He also informed that around 1500 Delegates including National and International Speakers are expected to attend the 19th UMI Conference & Exhibition.
The conference will be inaugurated by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, in the presence of Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra, Hon’ble Minister, Housing & Urban Development, Government of Odisha, and other dignitaries.
The two-day event will bring together national and international experts, policymakers, senior officials from Central and State Governments, Managing Directors of Metro Rail Companies, Chief Executives of Transport Undertakings, technology and service providers, professionals and academicians.
As part of the conference ​an exhibition
, comprising display of best practices in urban transport in India and abroad, latest urban transport technologies and services and in other related fields, will be organized . It will be inaugurated by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India in presence of Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra, Hon’ble Minister, Housing & Urban Development, Odisha and other dignitaries on day one and will continue for next 2 days. 28 exhibitors from Govt. of Odisha, Metro Rail Companies, public and private sector will participate.
Research Symposium
is being held in four sessions to encourage young research scholars and PhD students to present their research work. A total of 46 research papers have been selected by Peer Group for presentation by 20 candidates and remaining 26 through poster presentation. The best three research papers selected by a jury will be given cash award of Rs. 25,000/- and certificates to all presenters
The Urban Mobility India Conference is an annual initiative of MoHUA under the National Urban Transport Policy (NUTP), 2006. The policy emphasises capacity building at the State and city levels and promotes equitable and sustainable urban transport systems. The conference facilitates the exchange of knowledge, experiences and best practices in urban mobility from India and across the world.
Participation of Government of Odisha
Speaking on the occasion, Smt. Usha Padhee, IAS, Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Odisha, highlighted the State Government’s commitment to sustainable urban development, improved urban mobility and efficient delivery of urban services. She emphasised that hosting the 19th Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition and the National Urban Conclave 2026 in Bhubaneswar reflects Odisha’s growing engagement in national-level discussions on urban transformation. She noted that the State is focused on strengthening urban infrastructure, promoting technology-driven transport solutions, improving accessibility and liveability, and fostering collaboration among stakeholders to build inclusive, sustainable and future-ready cities.
The two events will provide a common platform for exchanging ideas, sharing experiences and discussing solutions to contemporary urban challenges. The conferences will bring together key stakeholders to deliberate on sustainable urban mobility, improved accessibility, effective urban governance and better delivery of urban services.
Odisha preparations and initiatives for the events:
•
PM e Bus Sewa launch:
The launch of PM e-Bus Sewa in Odisha is planned during the events, advancing cleaner public transport and improved urban connectivity.
•
Odisha initiatives to be launched and released:
The programme includes the ANKUR Handbook, Odisha Town Planning Handbooks and the Policy on Government and Privately Owned Public Spaces for Odisha, highlighting the State’s work on urban capacity building, planned growth and accessible public spaces.
•
CRUT pavilion:
A dedicated CRUT pavilion will showcase Odisha’s public transport journey through Ama Bus, electric mobility, feeder services, women’s participation and technology-enabled passenger convenience and safety.
•
Sand art by Sudarsan Pattnaik:
A special sand art installation by renowned sand artist Sudarsan Pattnaik will connect Odisha’s cultural heritage with sustainable and inclusive mobility, highlighting pedestrians, cyclists and accessible streets for all.
•
BMC preparations:
Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation is undertaking city cleanliness, sanitation, beautification and public-space improvements to welcome delegates. Exposure visits will showcase initiatives in waste processing and resource recovery, shelters and rehabilitation, inclusive neighbourhood development, urban greenery and citizen services.
•
BDA preparations:
Bhubaneswar Development Authority is supporting the event preparations through exhibition displays and exposure visits highlighting planned urban development, housing, town planning schemes, public transport infrastructure, parks and rejuvenated public spaces.
•
Heritage walks and cycling activities:
Special Ekamra Walks and a cycle trail will offer delegates an opportunity to experience Bhubaneswar’s heritage and public spaces while promoting walking, cycling and non-motorised mobility.
•
Odisha experience sharing:
Odisha will contribute its experience in bus modernisation, regional mobility planning and urban service delivery, linking the national deliberations with local implementation and citizen needs.
•
Mission Shakti:
Mission Shakti’s participation will showcase products made by women’s self-help groups, highlighting women’s entrepreneurship and community-led livelihoods in Odisha.
•
Utkalika:
Utkalika will showcase Odisha’s rich handicraft traditions, offering delegates a glimpse of the State’s craftsmanship and artisan heritage.
•
Boyanika:
Boyanika will showcase Odisha’s handloom legacy, celebrating the skills of its weavers and the diversity of its textile traditions.
•
Koraput Coffee:
Koraput Coffee will introduce delegates to Odisha’s distinctive coffee, highlighting the produce and livelihoods associated with the Koraput region.

title: As A Follow-Up to The Departmental Summit on Water 2026, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Organised Virtual Conference on Convergence of JJM 2.0 With 16th Finance Grants for Rural water Supply and Strengthening of O&M Systems
subtitle: Secretary, DDWS calls for stronger Panchayat-led planning, interdepartmental coordination and sustainable financing of rural water supply infrastructure
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The
Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti
, today organised the
fourth virtual conference with States and Union Territories
as part of a series of thematic consultations being held in follow-up to the
Departmental Summit on Water 2026 held on 1-2 September 2026
. The conference focused on strengthening convergence between
Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0
and 16th Finance Commission to advance source sustainability, water security and Gram Panchayat-led planning for sustainable rural drinking water service delivery.
The virtual conference brought together senior officials from State PHEDs/Rural Water Supply Departments, Panchayati Raj Departments and representatives from the Ministries of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India and National Informatics Centre. States rural water supply departments including Karnataka, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh shared best practices and field experiences on leveraging Finance Commission grants for strengthening rural water supply systems, improving O&M arrangements, enhancing community participation and strengthening local governance mechanisms.
Addressing in the conference,
Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS
, stated that with the extension of JJM 2.0, the focus now shifts from infrastructure creation to ensuring functionality, sustainability and quality service delivery. He emphasised that the true measure of success lies not merely in asset creation but in ensuring that rural households continue to receive reliable and safe drinking water through well-maintained and financially sustainable systems.
Shri Meena underlined the pivotal role of
Gram Panchayats
in rural water governance and noted that the
73rd Constitutional Amendment
places drinking water and sanitation among the key responsibilities of local self-governments. He stressed that Gram Panchayats must take leadership in preparing comprehensive annual O&M plans, mobilising local resources, managing service delivery and ensuring accountability for water supply infrastructure created under JJM and other programmes.
Referring to the
16th Finance Commission framework
, he highlighted that tied grants provide a significant opportunity to strengthen the sustainability of drinking water and sanitation services at the grassroots level. He noted that of the total Rural Local Body (RLB) grants recommended by the 16th Finance Commission, a substantial share has been earmarked for water and sanitation-related activities. He emphasised that these grants should be utilised primarily for operation and maintenance, source sustainability, water quality management, service delivery improvements and strengthening local institutional capacity rather than creation of new infrastructure where existing assets require maintenance and support.
The Secretary focused on
three key pillars
of sustainable financing for rural water supply systems such as effective utilisation of Finance Commission grants, ii. convergence with other available programmes and iii. schemes, and progressive strengthening of user-charge collection mechanisms.
Referring to successful examples from several States, he encouraged States and Gram Panchayats to adopt sustainable revenue models that support recurring O&M expenditure and reduce dependence on a single funding source. He also stressed the growing role of Gram Panchayats in the management of sanitation and solid waste systems and highlighted the need for local bodies to plan comprehensively for both drinking water and sanitation services. He noted that adequate provisions must be made for repairs, leak management, pump maintenance, chlorination, water-quality surveillance, electricity expenditure and staffing arrangements required for uninterrupted service delivery.
Emphasising capacity building as a critical requirement, Shri Meena called upon States to utilise resources available under the
Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA)
and other programmes for training Panchayat representatives and local functionaries. He urged States to translate and disseminate Operation and Maintenance Manuals in local languages and ensure that Panchayats clearly understand the permissible activities, funding mechanisms and reporting requirements under the Finance Commission framework.
He called upon to strengthen coordination between Rural Water Supply Departments, Panchayati Raj Institutions and Rural Development Departments at the State, district and Gram Panchayat levels. He noted that the simultaneous implementation of
JJM 2.0
,
VB-G RAM G
, and the
16th Finance Commission cycle
provides a unique opportunity to institutionalise sustainable water governance through integrated planning and coordinated implementation.
Ms. Kritika Kulhari, Deputy Secretary, NJJM made a detailed presentation on the
16th Finance Commission Grants and utilisation of tied grants for water and sanitation
, outlining the grant structure, release conditions, reporting requirements, permissible activities and planning framework. Participants were informed that the total Rural Local Body allocation under the 16th Finance Commission exceeds ₹4.35 lakh crore, with nearly ₹1.74 lakh crore earmarked for water management and sanitation over the award period. The presentation highlighted that priority should be accorded to operation and maintenance of existing assets, lifecycle-based planning, preventive maintenance, community ownership and digital accountability through prescribed platforms.
Shri Vipul Ujwal, Director, Ministry of Panchayati Raj
, made a detailed presentation on
GPDP planning, release modalities and utilisation of Finance Commission Grants for rural water supply O&M
. He emphasised that sustainable service delivery requires integration of three critical elements -
Requirements, Resources and Responsibilities (RRR)
. He explained how Gram Panchayats should identify service gaps, estimate annual O&M requirements, assess available financial resources and integrate these priorities into the Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP). He further highlighted the growing importance of Own Source Revenue (OSR), user-charge collection and performance-based grants in strengthening Panchayat finances and ensuring sustainable service delivery.
The conference also featured a technical presentation by
NIC, Ministry of Panchayati Raj
, on the
eGramSwaraj portal and its reporting modules
. The session explained how Gram Panchayats can integrate planning, implementation, geo-tagging, expenditure reporting, asset management and monitoring through the digital platform. title: “Strong States Contribute to a Strong Union; Cooperative Governance Transforms Constitutional Ideals into Public Good”: Vice-President
subtitle:
Law Commission of India Brings Centre and States Together to Advance Collaborative Law Reform at National Conference on ‘Co-operative Federalism and Law Reforms:

National and State Perspectives’

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Outlines Four Priorities for Law Reform: Continuous Institutional Dialogue, Evidence-Based and Participatory Law Reform, Technology with Human Oversight and

Citizen-Centric Legal Design

Law Commission Chairperson Proposes “Citizen Friction Test” to Assess Time, Cost and Procedural Burden of Laws
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 5:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 23rd Law Commission of India today convened a National Conference on “Co-operative Federalism and Law Reforms: National and State Perspectives” at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, bringing together national and State law-reform institutions, jurists, former judges, legal scholars, policymakers, law students, members of the Bar and academia to strengthen dialogue and collaboration on law reform within India’s federal framework.
Inaugurating the Conference, the Vice-President said that India’s greatest strength lies in its unity in diversity, with the Constitution providing the framework to balance the strength of the Union with the responsibilities and legitimate autonomy of the States. He emphasised that the true strength of Indian federalism lies in respecting diversity while working towards common national objectives.
Highlighting the importance of legal reforms in achieving Viksit Bharat @2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that development must be supported by sound laws, transparent institutions, efficient administration and justice for all. Stressing that cooperative federalism in law reforms does not imply uniformity in every matter, the Vice-President said that the Union and States must work together where their constitutional responsibilities converge, while preserving the States’ legitimate space to address their specific needs. He called for stronger coordination among the Law Commission of India, State Law Commissions and State Law Departments through inter-State consultations, sharing of best practices and systematic review of outdated laws.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, said that law reform must combine national constitutional objectives with the social, economic and administrative experience of the States. He identified four priorities for the way forward: continuous institutional dialogue; evidence-based and participatory law reform; technology with human oversight; and citizen-centric legal design.
Referring to Article 1 of the Constitution and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s exposition in the Constituent Assembly, Shri Meghwal recalled the conception of India as a Union of States. He also referred to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s emphasis on the spirit of “Team India” and said that national perspectives provide direction towards shared constitutional objectives, while States bring their social, economic and administrative experience to the reform process. He further stressed the need to bring together ease of doing business, ease of living and ease of justice, while ensuring that simplification does not compromise rights and safeguards. Summing up the way forward, he said, “Sashakt Rajya, Sashakt Bharat, Saral Kanoon, Sulabh Nyaya — Yahi Hamari Saajha Disha Ho.”
Justice (Retd.) Dinesh Maheshwari, Chairperson, Law Commission of India, called for a more structured framework of collaboration between national and State law-reform institutions, including a common law-reform docket, joint studies and post-enactment review. He proposed a “citizen friction test” to assess whether a proposed law reduces the time, cost and procedural burden on citizens, and suggested that participating Law Commissions and equivalent bodies could, within about six months, place their first joint issue papers before their respective governments for consideration.
Justice Maheshwari said, “For the citizen, justice is not divided between the Lists of the Seventh Schedule. The expectation of justice is one, and so must be our commitment to its delivery.”
Welcoming participants from across the country, Dr. Anju Rathi Rana ILS, Member Secretary, Law Commission of India, said the Commission can serve as a bridge, ensuring that valuable legal experience does not remain confined within institutional or geographical boundaries. Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s emphasis on “Nagrik Devo Bhava” and more recently his description of the Jan Vishwas reforms as strengthening “a trust-based framework that empowers our citizens,” she said, “The ultimate unit of law reform is not the statute. It is the citizen.” Calling for sustained engagement between national and State law-reform institutions, she added, “The task is not to make every State think alike. It is to ensure that no State has to think alone.”
The inaugural session was followed by two technical sessions on “Reforms in Law: Needs and Methods” and “Allocated Powers, Shared Goals: Drafting the Future with Collaborative Jurisprudence”. The sessions examined approaches to responsive and evidence-based law reform, including how ideas such as Nyaya, Kartavya and Lok Kalyan may inform context-sensitive reform consistent with equality, liberty and dignity. They also considered mechanisms for greater collaboration and exchange of experience between national and State law-reform institutions, while respecting State autonomy and regional diversity.
The day-long Conference brought national and State institutions into a common conversation on making law reform more responsive and attuned to the realities of implementation across India’s diverse jurisdictions. The Conference concluded with a valedictory session.

title: AgriVoltaics World Conference 2026
subtitle: Day 2 Highlights State Leadership, Next-Gen Technology, and Blended Finance Mechanisms
ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 7:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The second day of the AgriVoltaics World Conference 2026 accelerated cross-sectoral engagement across state policy leadership, technological innovation, private sector engagement and climate finance solutions.
A dedicated ministerial track, co-organised by the International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) and the Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW), brought together State Ministers of Energy and Agriculture from Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Bihar to present state-level approaches for accelerating agrivoltaic deployment. The session served as a platform for states to showcase investment opportunities, highlighting innovative land-use models, state-level tariff incentives, and adaptation of the PM-KUSUM scheme to local agricultural conditions and crop profiles. Discussions underscored the growing role of sub-national governments in creating enabling environments for agrivoltaic investments.
Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma, Minister of Energy, Uttar Pradesh, highlighted the state’s vast agricultural base, diverse cropping patterns and expanding solar infrastructure as key advantages for agrivoltaics. He emphasised that generating solar power alongside cultivation would optimise land use and create an additional income stream for farmers. Highlighting Uttar Pradesh’s progress in rooftop solar and grid infrastructure, he noted that Green Energy Corridor-III would further strengthen power evacuation for renewable energy projects. He also stressed the need for financing models and technologies suited to small and marginal farmers, who account for nearly 80% of agricultural holdings in the state. Inviting investors to explore these opportunities, he said, “The potential for agrivoltaics is enormous. Those who wish to be associated with agrivoltaics need to look towards Uttar Pradesh.” He also assured investors of the state’s support for grid connectivity and power evacuation.
Shri Surya Pratap Shahi, Minister of Agriculture, Uttar Pradesh, highlighted the state’s plan to solarise all 16 lakh agricultural tubewells whose electricity bills have been waived, supported by dedicated grid infrastructure. He emphasised that farmers’ land ownership rights must be protected and called for structured training on crop selection and agrivoltaic practices. He proposed leveraging Krishi Vigyan Kendras, agricultural universities and technical institutions to build farmers’ capacity, while integrating agrivoltaics with agricultural diversification and existing farmer-support initiatives. Highlighting the central role of farmers in the state’s economy, he said, “The agriculture of Uttar Pradesh and its farmers are, in a way, the lifeblood of our economic system.” He also assured farmers that ownership of their land would remain protected.
Shri Rakesh Shukla, Minister of New and Renewable Energy, Madhya Pradesh, highlighted the state’s efforts to advance agrivoltaics, solar deployment and battery storage as part of its farmer-welfare agenda, with 2026 being observed as the Year of Farmer Welfare in Madhya Pradesh. He noted that cultivation beneath solar panels had begun at several locations and that the state was progressing with battery-storage projects, for which the tendering process had been completed. He also highlighted Madhya Pradesh’s wider renewable energy infrastructure, including the Omkareshwar project. Emphasising the state’s progress in agrivoltaics, he said, “In the agricultural sector, we have some plants where farming takes place beneath solar panels. Such projects have begun at a few locations in Madhya Pradesh, and we are continuously progressing in this direction, including in battery storage, for which we have also completed the tendering process.”
Shri Shailesh Kumar Mandal, Minister of Energy, Bihar, highlighted the state’s efforts to strengthen agricultural electricity infrastructure through feeder separation and solarisation. He noted that Bihar had advanced work on approximately 2,700 agricultural feeders, with the state government approving financial support for their solarisation. Emphasising Bihar’s longstanding familiarity with solar energy and its commitment to expanding renewable energy access, he said, “Solar energy and sunlight are not new concepts in Bihar; this tradition has existed there for centuries.” He reiterated the state government’s commitment to taking forward agricultural feeder solarisation through an innovative approach.
Shri Vijay Kumar Sinha, Minister of Agriculture, Bihar, highlighted agrivoltaics as an opportunity to enhance farmers’ incomes, promote crop diversification and generate rural employment. He emphasised the need to strengthen research, farmer awareness and training through collaboration among agricultural institutions, financial institutions and energy enterprises. He also highlighted Bihar’s contribution to the country’s workforce as an opportunity to support wider adoption and implementation of agrivoltaics. He said, “A large pool of workers comes from Bihar and contributes to the workforce across the country. Many states rely on this workforce from Bihar.”
Shri Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo, Deputy Chief Minister, Odisha, announced that the state is finalising its dedicated Agrivoltaics Policy 2026, with a target of 1 GW by 2030. The proposed policy will require at least 90% of project sites to remain cultivable, safeguard farmer consent and crop insurance, and allow farmers to own projects or lease their land while continuing cultivation. To attract investment, Odisha plans to provide 25-year power purchase agreements through GRIDCO, grid connectivity and investment incentives. Highlighting the policy’s importance for investors, he said, “It gives investors certainty: 25 years of PPA with GRIDCO, an offtake guarantee, grid connectivity and the freedom of open access and competitive use.” He also announced that Odisha is finalising its dedicated Agrivoltaics Policy 2026, positioning the state to establish a policy framework specifically for agrivoltaics.
The Agrivoltaics Pitch-Hub was curated by the National Solar Energy Federation of India (NSEFI) where early-stage innovators and start-ups pitched bankable, dual-use agrivoltaic solutions before an expert jury comprising national institutes (NISE, NIBE), venture capitalists, and industry leaders.
Fraunhofer ISE and Sunseed APV demonstrated next-generation solutions, including advanced solar tracking systems, dynamic panel tilting, semi-transparent photovoltaic (PV) modules, and micro-climate soil sensors engineered specifically for tropical and arid conditions.
Hosted by the Indo-German Chamber of Commerce, the dialogue brought together Indian and international developers, including NTPC Green Energy, First Solar, and leading European firms to discuss supply chain localisation, standards development, and market certainty.
An executive roundtable convened representatives from multilateral development banks, financial institutions, and commercial lenders, including the World Bank, KfW, European Investment Bank, and IREDA.
Participants examined financial mechanisms needed to accelerate agrivoltaic deployment, including risk-mitigation instruments, concessional lending facilities, and blended finance structures capable of mobilising private investment at scale.
Bringing a vital youth perspective to the global stage, acclaimed actress and UNDP India Youth Champion Sanjana Sanghi joined the Conference for an exclusive fireside chat. Sanghi advocated for youth-led community strategies and spotlighted the intersection of food security, renewable energy, and youth mobilisation. She emphasised how agrivoltaics contributes to multiple UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) while directly empowering and securing livelihoods for rural youth.
The day concluded with an interactive Digital Poster Gallery, showcasing operational agrivoltaic projects and lessons from global case studies, providing participants with practical insights into implementation and scale-up strategies.

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Indian Railways has achieved an all-time record in coal loading, registering a 22.5% growth in October 2026 up to 18th October compared with the corresponding period last year. Coal loading during this period increased by 87 rakes per day over October 2025, reflecting the continued efforts to ensure reliable coal supplies to thermal power plants across the country.
During the first half (H1) of FY 2026-27, Indian Railways dispatched an average of 430 coal rakes per day to thermal power plants, registering a 7.1% increase over the corresponding period last year. The momentum continued in September 2026, when coal rake dispatches increased by 14% per day compared with September 2025.
The sustained pace of coal transportation comes amid rising energy consumption and increased demand for coal-based power generation due to higher industrial production and deficient rainfall in some parts of the country.
Consistent coal evacuation has helped maintain steady coal stocks at thermal power plants, supporting reliable power generation across the country. Indian Railways is working in close coordination with the Ministry of Coal to ensure efficient coal evacuation. It is also coordinating with the Ministry of Power to sustain coal transportation and supply, helping maintain adequate coal stocks at thermal power plants and meet the country’s energy requirements.
