title: World Entering an Era of AI-Guided, Gene-Driven Precision Medicine; India Emerging Among Frontline Providers: Dr. Jitendra Singh at SRIHER Convocation, Chennai
subtitle:
Young Doctors Will Have the Privilege of Using Enabling Technologies, along with the Challenge of Integrating Them Optimally with Clinical Practice: Dr. Jitendra Singh

India’s Advances in Indigenous Vaccines, Gene Therapy and Medical Research Reflect Growing Healthcare Capabilities, says Dr. Jitendra Singh

Rising Lifestyle Diseases Among Young People Make Prevention a Critical Healthcare Priority: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Dr. Jitendra Singh Invites Sri Ramachandra Institute to Expand Collaboration in Genomics, Biomanufacturing and Nuclear Medicine
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 4:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh, who is also a Professor of Medicine and Diabetes, today said that the world is entering an era of AI-guided, gene-driven precision medicine, with India emerging among the front-line providers of advanced healthcare solutions.
Addressing the 42nd Convocation, as chief guest, before awarding Medical degrees at Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research (SRIHER), Chennai, he said the next generation of medical professionals would have the privilege of using enabling technologies while facing the challenge of integrating them optimally with clinical practice. He stressed that the future of medicine would depend on combining technological advances with sound clinical judgement, while strengthening preventive healthcare to address the growing incidence of lifestyle diseases among younger people.
The Minister addressed the graduating students, faculty members and other dignitaries in the presence of Chancellor V. R. Venkatachalam, Pro-Chancellor R. V. Singhrutawarand other senior members of the institution. Congratulating undergraduate, postgraduate and super-specialty graduates, as well as gold medallists, Dr. Jitendra Singh expressed satisfaction at the institution’s growth and its contribution to medical education and research. He also conveyed his wishes for the speedy recovery of Vice-Chancellor Dr. Uma, who was unable to attend.
Drawing on his experience as a clinician spanning nearly four decades, Dr. Jitendra Singh traced the transformation of medical practice, from an earlier focus on communicable diseases to the growing burden of lifestyle-related disorders such as diabetes and cardiovascular diseases. He said that both communicable and non-communicable diseases continue to challenge healthcare systems, even as increasing life expectancy brings new medical demands. The emergence of chronic conditions at younger ages makes prevention, early intervention and long-term disease management increasingly important.
The Minister said that Diabetes and cardiovascular diseases, once more commonly associated with older age groups, are increasingly affecting younger people. A person developing diabetes at the age of 30 may have to live with its consequences for several decades, he said, making the protection of vital organs and prevention of complications essential responsibilities for doctors, families and patients. He stressed that preventing long-term disorders among young people is critical to protecting India's human potential and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
Referring to the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, genomics and other frontier technologies, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that tomorrow’s medical professionals would practise in an environment increasingly shaped by AI-assisted healthcare and gene-driven precision medicine. He said these technologies would open new possibilities for diagnosis, treatment and personalised care, while placing a corresponding responsibility on doctors to integrate them effectively into clinical practice. The challenge, he said, would be to make optimal use of emerging technologies while preserving the clinical orientation and judgement essential to patient care.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India has made significant progress in indigenous medical research and is increasingly contributing to global healthcare innovation. Referring to India's development of an indigenous DNA vaccine against COVID-19, he spoke about the country's growing capabilities in vaccine research, including ongoing work on diseases such as dengue and malaria. He also referred to advances in gene therapy for haemophilia, demonstrating how Indian research institutions are contributing to the development of solutions for complex medical conditions.
The Minister also referred to indigenous drug development, including nafithromycin for the treatment of community-acquired bacterial pneumonia, and advances in nuclear medicine research involving conditions such as acute lymphoblastic leukaemia and fatty liver disease. These developments, he said, reflect the expanding capacity of India's scientific and medical institutions to pursue new therapeutic approaches and strengthen the country's contribution to healthcare research.
Emphasising the importance of translating scientific advances into clinical outcomes, Dr. Jitendra Singh invited SRIHER to expand its engagement with national research initiatives in emerging fields such as genomics, biomanufacturing and nuclear medicine. He said collaboration between government research institutions, universities, hospitals and industry can help combine scientific expertise with clinical experience, accelerate innovation and facilitate the development of effective and affordable healthcare solutions.
The Minister referred to the growing opportunities for research and innovation in advanced scientific fields, including nuclear medicine, and encouraged the institution to build on its research capabilities, clinical expertise and startup ecosystem. He said closer collaboration between researchers, medical professionals and technology developers would be important in advancing new therapies, medical technologies and precision healthcare.
Speaking about the potential of genomics, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that integrating genomic information with clinical outcomes could help doctors increasingly tailor treatment to individual patients, taking into account their genetic profiles, lifestyles and environmental factors. As precision medicine advances, he said, medical professionals would need to combine emerging scientific knowledge with clinical experience to ensure that new technologies translate into meaningful improvements in patient care.
Concluding his address, the Minister stressed that preventing long-term disorders, particularly those increasingly affecting younger people, must become a collective national priority. subtitle:

Sonowal pitches India's growth story to Polish business leaders calls for “trusted supply chains”

Let us invest, innovate and develop together: Sonowal at India-Poland Business Forum
ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW) Sarbananda Sonowal
urged Polish companies to “build, innovate and invest in India” rather than only sell to it, as he pitched the country's growth story to business leaders from both nations.
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal delivered the keynote address at the India-Poland Business Forum here today which was also attended by
Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk
. Sonowal recalled that
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's
visit to Poland in August 2024 lifted ties to a strategic partnership.
“When Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Poland in August 2024, he and Prime Minister Tusk elevated our relations to a Strategic Partnership. They did so with a clear conviction: the India-Poland relationship must not only be strong in diplomacy; it must also be strong in business, technology, investment and innovation,” said Sarbananda Sonowal.
The aim now, he said, is for the relationship to be as strong in business, technology, investment and innovation as it is in diplomacy.
"India offers the scale of a large and growing market, the skills of a young and talented workforce, and the trust of a democracy committed to reform, enterprise and openness," Sonowal said.
Sonowal argued that the two economies fit together. Poland, he said, has strengths in engineering, machinery, mining technologies, transport, environmental solutions and advanced manufacturing. India has the market, talent and manufacturing base to give those capabilities scale. "My message to Polish companies is: do not only sell to India. Build in India. Develop solutions in India. Find Indian partners. And, use India as a platform for growth,"
Sonowal
said.
Sonowal cited that India, under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has set an ambitious target to generate 500 GW of non-fossil fuel power capacity by 2030, to put forth a strong Climate Action step by the country. He put the investment needed at roughly 280 billion to 300 billion euros, with openings for equipment makers, storage, power grids, green hydrogen, recycling and environmental technology. Poland's experience in mining, critical minerals and clean energy could help, Sonowal said.
On technology, Sonowal noted that Indian IT companies have made Poland a base for their European operations and employ about 10,000 people there. He said the next step should go beyond IT services, into artificial intelligence, quantum computing, 5G applications, digital infrastructure, smart manufacturing and space.
The Union
Minister proposed a Startup Bridge, an Innovation Corridor and an AI and Quantum Dialogue to link businesses, researchers and innovators in both countries. Trade between the two countries has reached $6.36 billion, and Indian investment in Poland exceeds $3 billion, Sonowal said. Polish companies are also active in India in packaging, manufacturing, waste-to-energy and electric mobility. He said the ambition should be larger than doubling trade by 2030.
"We should create together. We should innovate together. We should invest together. We should build trusted supply chains together. And we should succeed together," Sonowal said.
He urged business leaders to see the India-EU free trade agreement as more than a trade pact. "View it as a partnership multiplier," he said. It opens a larger window into the Indian market for Polish firms, he said, and widens European opportunities for Indian ones.
Sonowal concluded by describing India’s philosophy of “Power to Empower”, stating that beyond the power to compete lies the power to collaborate. “India’s growth can create opportunities for Poland. Poland’s capabilities can add strength to India. And together, our businesses can create solutions for the world,” he said.

title: Union Minister Shri Jayant Chaudhary Rings the Iconic NSE Bell and Marks NSDC’s Debut on NSE Social Stock Exchange, Opening New Avenues for Financing Skill Development and Global Employment
subtitle:
NABARD subscribes ₹4 crore to NSDC's maiden Zero Coupon Zero Principal issue; initiative to support international employment pathways for 600 rural youth from Madhya Pradesh

Innovative ₹11.25 crore programme integrates social investment, beneficiary participation and outcome-linked funding from the Government of Madhya Pradesh

Youth to receive Japanese and German language training for employment opportunities in Japan and Germany

Shri Jayant Chaudhary calls for greater participation of financial institutions and industry in outcome-oriented skilling initiatives
ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Govt of India, marked the National Skill Development Corporation's (NSDC) debut on the Social Stock Exchange (SSE) platform of the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Mumbai and participated in the bell-ringing ceremony. Through this programme, we are bringing together government funds, Private CSR, Retail investor Capital, and specialised training capabilities around a common objective of sustainable livelihood.
The occasion marked NSDC's maiden issuance of Zero Coupon Zero Principal (ZCZP) instruments, with the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) subscribing ₹4 crore towards an innovative skilling and global employment initiative. The programme will support 600 young people from economically weaker Other Backward Classes (OBC) households in Madhya Pradesh, preparing them for international employment opportunities.
The ceremony was attended by Smt. Krishna Gaur, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Backward Classes and Minorities Welfare, Government of Madhya Pradesh; Shri Mangal Prabhat Lodha, Minister for Skills, Employment, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, Government of Maharashtra; Smt. Manisha Verma, Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Maharashtra; Smt. Manisha Sensarma, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India; Shri Ashishkumar Chauhan, MD & CEO, National Stock Exchange (NSE); Shri Arunkumar Pillai, Chief Executive Officer, National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC); Dr. Shaji Krishnan V., Chairman, NABARD; and Shri Alok Shriram, Managing Director, DCM Shriram International Ltd., along with representatives from partner organisations. The event highlighted the growing role of social finance and collaborative institutional frameworks in expanding access to quality training, sustainable livelihoods and global workforce opportunities.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Govt of India said: “India’s growth must be matched by investment in its people. Government can create the enabling framework, but financing development at scale requires public institutions, private funders and donors to work together. The Social Stock Exchange connects this collective commitment with credible projects, transparency and verifiable outcomes. I congratulate NSDC, NABARD, NSE, the Government of Madhya Pradesh and all contributors for building a partnership that turns investment in skills into global employment opportunities and sustainable livelihoods.”
Smt. Krishna Gaur, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Backward Classes and Minorities Welfare, Government of Madhya Pradesh, said: "The Government of Madhya Pradesh is committed to expanding opportunities for young people from backward classes, particularly those who face financial and social barriers in accessing quality training and employment. This partnership with NSDC creates an opportunity for 600 youth from our State to acquire internationally relevant skills and prepare for employment in Japan and Germany. We are pleased to support a model where government funding is connected with successful placement outcomes. We believe this initiative can provide a valuable pathway towards economic independence and improved livelihoods for participating families."
Innovative financing model linking investment with employment outcomes
The programme, with an estimated outlay of ₹11.25 crore, adopts a blended-financing structure that combines three complementary sources of funding. Beneficiary participation will account for 15 per cent of the programme cost, 35 per cent will be supported through financing mobilised on the Social Stock Exchange, and the remaining 50 per cent will be provided by the Government of Madhya Pradesh upon successful international placement of candidates.
The outcome-linked component is structured under a bilateral Social Impact Bond framework between NSDC and the Government of Madhya Pradesh, aligning public expenditure with measurable employment outcomes. The State Government will also support candidate mobilisation, residential training infrastructure and language laboratories.
The ZCZP framework enables eligible social-purpose organisations to mobilise resources without conventional interest or principal repayment obligations, with emphasis on transparent deployment of funds and reporting of social outcomes.
Speaking on the significance of the initiative, Smt. Manisha Sensarma, Additional Secretary, MSDE, said, "From a public-policy perspective, the significance of this initiative lies in its financing architecture and accountability framework. It demonstrates how public resources can be combined with institutional and social investment to support clearly defined development outcomes. The Ministry welcomes NSDC's efforts to explore innovative financing instruments while maintaining strong governance, transparent reporting and measurable results. The experience from this programme can provide useful lessons for designing and scaling future outcome-oriented skilling interventions."
Strengthening institutional partnerships
NABARD's participation represents an important convergence between rural development finance and the expanding opportunities available through international workforce mobility. The initiative seeks to support economically weaker rural households by creating pathways to higher earning potential, increased household savings and sustained livelihood improvement.
Dr. Shaji Krishnan V., Chairman, NABARD, said: "NABARD's participation in Social Stock Exchange issue reflects our commitment to exploring innovative development-finance models. We hope this initiative will encourage greater institutional and private sector participation while demonstrating the potential of innovative financing models to deliver measurable social impact. Ultimately, the true measure of development finance lies not in the amount of capital mobilised, but in how effectively it is translated into opportunities, sustainable livelihoods and lasting improvements in people’s lives."
Shri Arunkumar Pillai, CEO, NSDC, said: "NSDC's debut on the Social Stock Exchange is an important step in our efforts to diversify financing for skill development and employment-linked interventions. Through this programme, we are bringing together government support, institutional capital and specialised training capabilities around a common objective of sustainable livelihoods. We are grateful to NABARD, NSE, the Government of Madhya Pradesh and our partners for their confidence and collaboration. Our focus will now be on effective implementation, verifiable outcomes and building a portfolio of initiatives that can attract greater participation in social financing."
“The initiative will prepare 300 candidates for employment opportunities in Japan and another 300 for Germany through residential foreign-language and employability training. The programme will focus on destination-specific readiness and employment opportunities across sectors including caregiving, hospitality, construction and manufacturing. Training will be delivered by NSDC International Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of NSDC,” he added.
The initiative is expected to provide participating candidates with access to international employment opportunities and enhanced earning potential. Indicative monthly earnings for successfully placed candidates are estimated at approximately ₹1–1.2 lakh in Japan and ₹1.1–3.2 lakh in Germany, depending on the job role and employment conditions.
NSDC's participation on the Social Stock Exchange forms part of its broader efforts to develop innovative, outcome-oriented financing models that complement government investment in skill development. By combining social investment with employment-linked public funding, the initiative seeks to establish a replicable framework for strengthening employability, expanding global workforce mobility and improving livelihood outcomes.
About NSDC
The National Skill Development Corporation works under the aegis of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of India. Through industry partnerships, innovative financing mechanisms and skill development initiatives, NSDC seeks to enhance employability, strengthen vocational training and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for India's youth.

Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, until October 28 Wednesday.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela is open to public at Farm Gate, Khanapara, Guwahati, from 11 A.M. onwards till 9 O’ Clock. He said the visitors are exploring the diverse range of traditional products to purchase the creations and support the artisans.
He said the Mela is bringing together artisans from across the country, including the North-Eastern States, to showcase India’s rich and diverse heritage of traditional handicrafts and handloom products.
The Official said a total of

, displaying approximately 40 varieties of handloom and handicraft products.
He said the event is providing participating artisans with a platform to exhibit and sell their products directly to visitors, establish connections with prospective customers and explore opportunities to expand their market reach.
By facilitating direct interaction between artisans and consumers, the Mela seeks to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and improve livelihood opportunities for participating artisans, he added.
The Official said the Guwahati edition features a wide range of traditional crafts and handloom products representing different regions of India.
The participation of artisans from the North-Eastern States, alongside those from other parts of the country, will provide visitors with an opportunity to appreciate the diversity of India’s artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship and cultural heritage, he added.
He said the event aims to also encourage greater appreciation of the skills and creativity of artisans whose work contributes to preserving traditional knowledge and craft practices.
The Official further said a key focus of the Mela is the promotion of
BHARAT-TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme)
, an initiative aimed at facilitating the marketing of products made by artisans belonging to the target groups through physical outlets and e-commerce platforms.
By promoting access to wider markets and digital channels, the initiative is aimed to strengthen market linkages, expand customer outreach and create additional opportunities for artisans to enhance their earnings.
It also supports the preservation and promotion of traditional arts and crafts by connecting artisans and their products with evolving consumer markets, he said.
The Shilp Samagam Mela (SSM-2026) is an important initiative of the Ministry to provide marketing support to artisans and beneficiaries associated with its three National Corporations: the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), and the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC).
The first edition of SSM 2026 concluded in Mysuru on October 19, with thousands of visitors thronging the nine days Mela at Dasara Exhibition Ground, Mysuru in Karnataka.
Guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s principle of
“Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas”
, the Mela is promotiong the economic empowerment of artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras and Denotified Tribes (DNTs).
The Mela is providing a dedicated platform for these communities to showcase their skills, market their products and strengthen their economic self-reliance through sustainable livelihood opportunities.
In addition to promoting the sale of traditional products, the Mela is creating awareness among visitors and participating communities about the welfare, financial assistance and development schemes implemented by the Ministry and its three National Corporations.
The initiative is complementing financial and developmental support with market-oriented interventions, enabling artisans to translate their traditional skills and craftsmanship into viable livelihood opportunities, the official said.
It is pertinent to mention that through initiatives such as Shilp Samagam Mela, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to advance its efforts towards the socio-economic empowerment of communities having financial constraints, by promoting entrepreneurship, facilitating market access and supporting sustainable livelihoods.
The Mela is enhancing the visibility of participating artisans, expanding awareness of their products and encouraging greater public engagement with India’s rich handloom and handicraft traditions.

The meeting was attended by Additional Chief Secretary, Home; Commissioner Secretary, Education; Secretary, Social Welfare Department; Secretary, Health; Director General, Social Welfare, Kashmir; Director, Social Welfare, Jammu; Head of Department, Psychiatry, Government Medical College, Srinagar; Secretary, SC/ST/OBC Boards, besides officers of other concerned departments.
Appreciating the UT Administration’s efforts to extend welfare interventions to the grassroots, the Union Secretary observed that the outreach undertaken across villages and panchayats reflected a strong commitment to inclusive welfare delivery. He particularly commended J&K’s coordinated campaign against the drug menace, noting that its whole-of-government approach had received nationwide appreciation and could serve as a successful model for other regions.
Expressing satisfaction over the progress of individual beneficiary-oriented schemes, the Union Secretary highlighted the importance of ensuring that interventions for students, senior citizens, destitute women and other vulnerable sections deliver meaningful outcomes. He advised the Administration to document first-hand beneficiary testimonies and showcase the thousands of success stories emerging from these initiatives to generate wider awareness and amplify their impact across the country.
Reviewing the rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging, Shri Pant encouraged the UT Administration to work towards achieving the ‘Begging-Free City’ status for its urban centres. He observed that the relatively small number of such persons could be addressed through focused rehabilitation, sustained support and collaboration with dedicated non-governmental organisations.
The Union Secretary also outlined key priorities and focus areas for the UT to facilitate the achievement of the Ministry’s objectives. He appreciated Chief Secretary Atal Dulloo for his continued guidance and mentoring of the J&K's Social Welfare Department, observing that its diverse mandate required close coordination across multiple departments for effective implementation.
Speaking on the occasion, Chief Secretary Atal Dulloo reaffirmed the Government’s unwavering commitment to inclusive growth, social justice and community empowerment. He emphasized that the UT Administration was committed to saturating the benefits of welfare schemes among all eligible and deserving beneficiaries, particularly those belonging to disadvantaged and underprivileged sections of society.
Further the Chief Secretary threw light on the population profile of various beneficiary groups in J&K, the welfare measures available for their upliftment and the legal, institutional and regulatory safeguards established to protect their rights and prevent atrocities, discrimination and harassment. He stressed the importance of coordinated efforts to ensure that the benefits of these interventions reach every eligible beneficiary.
On this occasion the Secretary, Social Welfare Department, Doifode Sagar Dattatray, presented a detailed appraisal of the progress achieved under various centrally sponsored and UT-level schemes, covering drug demand reduction, educational scholarships, senior citizen welfare, rehabilitation, sanitation-worker safety, community development and legal protection for vulnerable groups.
Under the Nasha Mukt J&K 100 Days Abhiyan, the Department reported extensive public outreach through coordinated efforts involving multiple departments. It was revealed that more than 7.21 million outreach events had been conducted across the UT with Addiction Treatment Facilities handling 66,594 outpatients, while the Department’s Drug De-addiction and Rehabilitation Centres providing care to 1,053 individuals.
On the enforcement front, it was given out that the Police had registered 1,187 FIRs and arrested 1,349 persons. With respect to financial investigations the meeting was apprised that the same resulted in the seizure or attachment of 125 immovable properties valued at ₹9,828.17 lakh and 60 movable assets worth ₹703.83 lakh belonging to drug traffickers. The meeting was informed that the proposed Rehabilitation and Socio-Economic Reintegration Scheme for Drug Abuse Victims, 2026, envisaging a structured three-year recovery framework.
On this occasion, Dr Arshad Hussain, Head of the Department of Psychiatry, GMC Srinagar, elaborated on J&K’s ‘Circle of Care’ approach to addressing substance use disorders. The three-dimensional strategy provides continuity of care from admission to de-addiction facilities through treatment, rehabilitation, social reintegration and long-term monitoring to support sustained recovery.
Moreover it was divulged that under the Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana, it was informed that 419 villages had been selected for development as model villages, of which 28 had been declared Adarsh Grams. The review emphasised the need for sustained interdepartmental coordination, effective beneficiary outreach, timely resolution of implementation bottlenecks and a stronger focus on documenting and publicising success stories to ensure that welfare interventions translate into tangible improvements in the lives of people across Jammu and Kashmir.

title: 1, 87,305 Candidates Trained and Placed 96,162 During 2020-21 to 2023-24 under PM-DAKSH Scheme
subtitle:
From 2024-25 onwards, PM-DAKSH Merged with PMKVY Scheme of MSDE

Evaluation Study Reports Over 90% of Beneficiaries Found Training Aligned with Career Goals and Local Labour Market Needs
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Pradhan Mantri Dakshata Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi (PM-DAKSH), a Central Sector Scheme, was launched during 2020-21 to provide skill training to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), De-notified Tribes (DNTs), and Safai Karamcharis, including Waste Pickers, through empanelled training institutes to encourage self-employment and wage-employment for their socio-economic development.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said the scheme was implemented by three Corporations of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE), namely, the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).
The Official said that from 2024-25 onwards, it was decided to merge PM-DAKSH with the PMKVY Scheme of MSDE. As PM-DAKSH was an additionality to PMKVY and all job roles for providing skill training were taken from the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) portal, which were also covered under PMKVY, PM-DAKSH was subsumed under PMKVY to avoid duplication, she added.
The Official said the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment releases funds to the Corporations, which reimburse training costs to institutes empanelled under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), as per the scheme guidelines and work order.
She said after training completion, institutes are required to provide wage-employment and/or self-employment to at least 70% of trained candidates. If this requirement is not met, the third instalment, amounting to 30% of the training cost, is forfeited. Training institutes are also mandated to maintain collaboration with relevant industries to facilitate employment opportunities for trained candidates. The three Corporations extend loan facilities and assistance to eligible youth from the target group in setting up their projects by providing handholding support, the Official added.
Against the total funds allotted for PM-DAKSH from 2020-21 to 2023-24 amounting to ₹276.47 crore, actual expenditure of ₹309.5 crore had been incurred till date. During 2020-21 to 2023-24, 1,87,305 candidates were trained and 96,162 candidates were placed, the Official said.
The Official further said the evaluation study of the PM-DAKSH Scheme shows strong relevance and learning effectiveness, with over 90% of beneficiaries reporting alignment of training with their career goals and local labour market needs, as well as achievement of intended learning outcomes. Impact results indicate non-material gains such as improved confidence, self-esteem and social recognition, particularly among women and marginalised groups. Sustainability outcomes are largely positive, with most beneficiaries continuing to use the skills acquired, expecting long-term income growth, reinvesting in development and feeling capable of maintaining improvements independently, the Official added.

title: NMBA Reaches Over 35 Crore People, Including Over 13.94 Crore Youth, 10.86 Crore Women, More Than 32 Lakh Educational Institutions Covered Under Outreach Activities
subtitle:
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Strengthens Community-Led Efforts Towards A Drug-Free India

The Country Will Collectively Succeed In Uprooting The Drug Trade From India By 31 December 2029: Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan under the Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment has reached more than 35 Crore people, including over 13.94 Crore youth and 10.86 Crore women, and engaged with more than 32 lakh plus educational institutions, as on date.
The Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah while speaking at the 3rd National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States and Union Territories, in New Delhi in September, said that by 31 December 2029, the country will collectively succeed in uprooting the drug trade from India. He emphasized the need for coordinated action, clear targets, accountability and a focus on dismantling drug networks. He also highlighted the importance of protecting young people from substance abuse as part of the national vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.
Launched on 15 August 2020, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan initially focused on 272 vulnerable districts and has since expanded its reach across the country. The campaign places particular emphasis on youth, women and communities, recognizing their role in preventing substance use and encouraging healthy lifestyles.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said these efforts demonstrate the importance of sustained public participation in building awareness and encouraging collective responsibility towards a drug-free society.
He said through awareness programmes, pledge campaigns, educational activities and collaboration with government departments and civil society stakeholders, NMBA seeks to bring the message of substance-use prevention closer to people in their everyday environments.
The educational institutions, youth clubs, women’s groups and local communities serve as important platforms for communicating the risks associated with substance use and encouraging early intervention, he added.
The Official further said the Ministry is strengthening community-led efforts to address substance use through the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), its flagship initiative for drug demand reduction. By mobilising young people, women, educational institutions, families and community stakeholders, the Abhiyaan seeks to build a society that is informed about the risks of substance use and supportive of prevention, treatment and recovery.
The initiative complements the Central Government’s broader efforts to combat the drug menace through a coordinated approach involving awareness, prevention, enforcement and rehabilitation.
While enforcement agencies work to disrupt drug trafficking and supply networks, NMBA addresses the demand-reduction dimension through awareness, community participation and access to support services. This complementary approach recognises that a sustainable response to substance use requires not only action against illicit drug networks but also informed communities, early prevention, accessible treatment and social reintegration.
Young people are central to NMBA’s strategy. The campaign encourages their active participation in awareness activities and community initiatives, enabling them to become advocates for healthy and substance-free lifestyles.
The broader national anti-narcotics roadmap has also underscored the importance of taking awareness efforts to schools, colleges and other institutions through Nashamukt Mitras. Such efforts complement NMBA’s focus on empowering individuals to share reliable information, challenge misconceptions and encourage their peers to seek help when required.
By promoting informed decision-making and constructive community engagement, the campaign aims to strengthen protective environments for young people and reduce the stigma associated with substance-use disorders.
NMBA adopts a comprehensive approach to drug demand reduction, encompassing prevention, assessment, treatment, rehabilitation, aftercare, public information dissemination and community awareness. This approach recognises that substance dependence requires appropriate support and that recovery is strengthened when individuals can access treatment and reintegrate into their families and communities with dignity.
The campaign also seeks to encourage compassionate attitudes towards individuals affected by substance use. Reducing stigma and promoting understanding can help people and their families seek assistance earlier, while community participation can support sustained recovery and social inclusion.
The NATIONAL DE-ADDICTION HELPLINE 14446 provides an avenue for individuals and families seeking information and assistance related to substance-use concerns.
As part of
Whole-of-Government
and
Whole-of-Society
approach, the fight against substance use requires sustained cooperation among government departments, educational institutions, healthcare and rehabilitation service providers, civil society organisations, families and citizens. NMBA’s community-based approach complements coordinated action by enforcement agencies by addressing awareness, prevention and the social dimensions of substance use.
For further information, awareness resources and campaign updates, the interested people may visit:
https://nmba.dosje.gov.in/
The campaign’s emphasis on collective responsibility aligns with the national resolve to protect the country’s youth and strengthen their contribution to India’s development. By combining public awareness with prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and community support, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan continues to advance the vision of a healthier, informed and drug-free India.

title: Factual Report on PM-DAKSH
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 11:49AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Pradhan Mantri Dakshata Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi (PM-DAKSH), a Central Sector Scheme, was launched during 2020-21 to provide skill training to SC, OBC, EWS, De-notified Tribes (DNTs), Safai Karamcharis including Waste Pickers through empanelled training institutes for encouraging self-employment and wage-employment for their socio-economic development.
The Scheme was implemented by three Corporations of Department of Social Justice & Empowerment (DoSJE) namely, National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and National Safai Karamcharis Finance & Development Corporation (NSKFDC).
DoSJE releases funds to the Corporations which reimburse the cost of training to the institutes who are empanelled under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) Scheme of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), as per Scheme Guidelines and Work Order. Post training completion, institutes are required to provide employment (wage and/or self-employment) to at least 70% of the trained candidates, failing which, the release of 3rd installment, i.e., 30% of the training cost is forfeited. Further, the training institutes are mandated to maintain collaboration with the relevant industries to facilitate employment opportunities for the trained candidates. The three Corporations extend loan facilities and assistance to the eligible youth of target group in setting up their projects by handholding them.
Against the total funds allotted for PM-DAKSH from 2020-21 to 2023-2024 of Rs.
276.47 crores, actual expenditure to the tune of Rs. 309.5 crores has been incurred till date.
The number of candidates trained and placed from 2020-21 to 2023-24 is 1,87,305 and 96,162 respectively.
Evaluation study of PM-DAKSH Scheme shows strong relevance and learning effectiveness, with over 90% of beneficiaries reporting alignment of training with career goals, local labour market needs and achievement of intended learning outcomes. Impact results indicate strong non-material gains such as improved confidence, self-esteem and social recognition, particularly among women and marginalized groups. Sustainability outcomes are largely positive, with most beneficiaries continuing to use acquired skills, expecting long-term income growth, reinvesting in development and feeling capable of maintaining improvements independently.
From 2024-25 onwards, it was decided to merge PM-DAKSH Scheme with PMKVY Scheme of MSDE, as the PM-DAKSH Scheme was an additionality to the PMKVY and all job roles for providing skill training were taken from the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) portal which were also covered under PMKVY. Therefore, to avoid any duplication, PM DAKSH was subsumed under PMKVY.

title: Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana
subtitle: Five More Years of Social Assistance, and a Wider Divyangjan Coverage
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 OCT 2026 2:17PM by PIB Delhi
content:
On 14 October 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme for five years, 2026-27 to 2030-31, with an outlay of
Rs 53,428 crore
. The programme becomes the
Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana
, and its four sub-schemes are renamed with it.  While the pension schemes for the old aged, widows and family benefit will continue in their existing forms, the Disability Pension has been revised.  It will now use the
40 per cent
benchmark disability of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016, in place of
80 per cent
. Its minimum eligibility age of
18 years
is removed, so eligibility now runs from birth. Central assistance rises to
Rs 375 a month for age 0-79 years
, and
Rs 625
at 80 years and above. Further, number of beneficiaries under the disability scheme has increased from
8.33 Lakhs
to
27.48
Lakhs.
A Renewed Programme for Social Assistance
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister, approved on 14 October 2026 the proposal of the Department of Rural Development to continue the National Social Assistance Programme for five years. The approval runs from 2026-27 to 2030-31 and carries an outlay of
Rs 53,428 crore
.
The approval covers three matters. It renames the programme and each of its sub-schemes. It revises the disability pension. It continues the other sub-schemes in their existing form.
The programme is now the
Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana
. Its four pension sub-schemes carry new names with it. The old age pension becomes the Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension Yojana. The widow pension becomes the Pradhan Mantri Vidhawa Pension Yojana. The disability pension becomes the Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana. The family benefit scheme becomes the Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana.
The old age pension, the widow pension and the family benefit scheme continue in their existing form. What changes is the disability pension, in its eligibility, its coverage and its rate of assistance.
What the National Social Assistance Programme Is
The programme was launched on
15 August 1995
. It gives effect to Article 41 of the Constitution, which directs the State to provide public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement. It is a fully funded centrally sponsored scheme and carries
100 per cent central assistance
. This ensures that a person below the poverty line receives at least the minimum support anywhere in the country. It covers both rural and urban areas, and the basic condition across its components is that the household is below the poverty line.
The programme has following components. Three are monthly pensions, for the old aged, for widows and for persons with disabilities. The fourth is a one-time family benefit on the death of a household's primary breadwinner.
States and Union Territories implement the schemes mainly through their social welfare departments, and in several States through the rural development, women and child development, revenue or labour departments. Gram Panchayats and municipalities take an active part in identifying beneficiaries, and payment is largely by direct benefit transfer.
The States and Union Territories also add their own top-up above the central rate. As on September 2026, those top-ups ranged from
Rs 50 to Rs 5700 per month
per beneficiary, giving an average monthly pension of around Rs 1100 in most States and Union Territories. The central rate is therefore the floor on which each State builds.
The programme covered about
3.09 crore beneficiaries
, against scheme-wise ceilings for each State and Union Territory. It was allocated Rs 9,652 crore for 2025-26, of which the disability pension accounted for Rs 290 crore. The approval of 14 October 2026 puts the programme's coverage at
3.20 crore beneficiaries
across all 36 States and Union Territories.
The Divyangjan Pension in Detail
The disability pension was introduced in February 2009, as the Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme. Section 2(o) of the National Trust Act 1999 defines severe disability as disability with
80 per cent
or more of one or more multiple disabilities. A person therefore had to be assessed at 80 per cent or above, and to be at least 18 years old, to receive the pension. Central assistance was Rs 300 a month for beneficiaries upto the age of 79, and Rs 500 a month for beneficiaries at age 80 and above.
Parliament then enacted the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016, to give effect to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. That Act sets a single working measure across its own entitlements. Section 2(r) defines a person with benchmark disability as a person with not less than
40 per cent
of a specified disability, as certified by the certifying authority.
The 2016 Act has necessitated changes in the eligibility criteria for the disability pension, linking it to benchmark disability of 40 per cent.
By its decision of 14 October 2026, the Government has brought the pension, now the
Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana
, onto that benchmark. It has removed the minimum age requirement, so that eligibility runs from birth. It has also raised central assistance to
Rs 375 a month
up to 79 years and
Rs 625 a month
at 80 years and above. The number of beneficiaries under this sub-scheme scheme has increased from
8.33 Lakhs to 27.48 Lakhs.
Revised guidelines carrying the eligibility criteria, the number of beneficiaries and the rates of assistance will be issued and implemented within three months.
Who the Decision Will Benefit
Three groups gain from the decision, and they are worth keeping distinct.
·
Persons certified between 40 and 79 per cent
, in households below the poverty line. The benchmark disability criterion approved on 14 October 2026 brings them within the pension.
·
Children, from birth.
A child with a certificate of benchmark disability in a household below the poverty line will benefit under the approved criteria, where the family earlier waited until the child turned 18.
·
Persons already receiving the pension.
They will receive the enhanced rates of Rs 375 and Rs 625 approved by the Government.
Three conditions are unchanged for all of them. A certificate of disability is still required, since benchmark disability under the 2016 Act is a percentage certified by the certifying authority. The household must still be below the poverty line, and the application route remains the State welfare department.
A Common Measure Across the Welfare System
Census 2011 recorded
2.68 crore
persons with disabilities in India, 2.21 per cent of the population. The Schedule to the 2016 Act specifies
21 types
of disabilites.
Since the 2016 Act came into force on 19 April 2017, its 40 per cent benchmark has governed disability entitlements in higher education, government employment, and land and housing. By the decision of 14 October 2026, the Government has brought its oldest social assistance programme, i.e., disability pension, in alignment with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016.
The revised guidelines will complete the picture, carrying the eligibility criteria, the number of beneficiaries and the rates of assistance under the Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana in one official document.

I am confident that Indian chemical manufacturers will take advantage of these opportunities to strengthen their presence in global supply chains.
The Prime Minister expressed hope that India Chem 2026 will encourage meaningful discussions and lead to partnerships that contribute to the long-term development of the sector.
Chief Ministers of Maharashtra Shri Devendra Fadnavis, Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav and Odisha Shri Mohan Charan Manjhi also addressed the gathering. They urged industry and business leaders to harness investment opportunities available in their states in the Chemicals and Petrochemicals sectors.
Shri Fadnavis said the Chemical Industry is very important for Maharashtra as it is providing employment to around Three Lakh people. He said Maharastra is preparing an investment friendly policy which is forward looking and based on ease of doing business.
Chief Ministers of Madhya Pradesh and Odisha invited industries to get benefit from their business friendly investment policies and infrastructure provided for Chemical Industry.
On the occasion,

said that the Chemical and Petrochemicals Industry occupies a pivotal position in meeting basic needs and improving quality of life.

Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojna (BHAVYA)
Rasayan Scheme for three new dedicated Chemical Parks. She urged the industry captains as well as the state governments to engage closely because states will play a very important role in realizing and implementing the scheme.
Shri Tejveer Singh , Secretary of the Department of Chemicals & Petrochemicals
, detailed the event's scope at the launch function.
He said the event will provide development of India's chemical and petrochemical sector to deliberate through focused group discussions on the way forward in various subsectors.
Shri Singh expressed hope that deliberations and interactions spread over the course of next 2 days it will provide a structured platform for business-to-business interactions.
On the occasion a knowledge paper prepared jointly by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) and Ernst & Young (EY) was released during the inaugural session of India Chem 2026.
Union Minister Shri Nadda also inaugurated an international India Chem 2026 exhibition at Bombay Exhibition Centre, NESCO which showcases a broad range of products, technologies, equipment and services across chemicals, petrochemicals, and process plant machinery and equipment.
Shri Nadda along with dignitaries also visited the stalls at the India Chem 2026 exhibition and interacted with industry leaders.
The three-day event, being organised by the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, in partnership with the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), comprises an international exhibition and conference. It brings together key stakeholders from the chemicals and petrochemicals sector, including industry leaders, policymakers, investors, researchers and international participants.
Held under the theme
“Advantage Bharat: An Emerging Global Chemicals Hub,”
India Chem 2026 provides a common platform for domestic and international stakeholders to exchange knowledge, forge strategic alliances, explore investment prospects and identify mutually beneficial business opportunities.
Strengthening economic cooperation with India, Japan has joined as the Partner Country for India Chem 2026, opening new avenues for collaboration in the chemicals and petrochemicals sector.
Maharashtra, Gujarat, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh are the Partner States, highlighting the growing role of Indian states in advancing the sector’s growth, investment and industrial development.
A key new feature of the 14th edition is the
India Chem Youth Innovation Challenge
, an initiative aimed at engaging young innovators, students and emerging entrepreneurs with the evolving needs of the chemicals and petrochemicals sector. The initiative seeks to encourage innovative, research-based and practical solutions to industry challenges.
The Indian chemical industry is projected to reach
USD 300 billion by 2030 and USD 1 trillion by 2040
. The sector's growth prospects are supported by rising domestic demand, expanding export opportunities, India's demographic dividend, relatively low per capita consumption and enabling government initiatives.

, more than
